title: Preserve arc geometry in PCB board outlines and cutouts
description: Preserves arc geometry in PCB board outlines and cutouts by reusing the existing BRep point_with_bulge schema, preventing loss of circular arc data during KiCad export.
body:
Parsing PCB board outlines and cutouts currently strips `bulge`, losing the original circular arc before KiCad export. Once only endpoints or sampled points remain, the exporter cannot reliably recover the authored curve.

Reuse the existing BRep `point_with_bulge` schema and `PointWithBulge` type for `pcb_board.outline`, polygon cutout `points`, and slot cutout `route`. This preserves the arc data while keeping existing point-only inputs valid.

Prior work: [#711 — Represent PCB path arcs with bulges](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/711) proposes the same representation for trace and graphic paths. It does not cover board outlines or cutouts. This PR fills that gap and targets `main` independently. Producer and KiCad exporter changes remain follow-up work.

Arc convention:

- Points use board coordinates in millimetres, with +X right and +Y up.
- `bulge = tan(signed_sweep_radians / 4)` describes the circular arc from a point to the next. Positive is counterclockwise; negative is clockwise. Zero or omission means a straight segment.
- Board outlines and polygon cutouts are closed: the final point connects to the first. Slot paths are open: the final point has no outgoing segment.

Validation:

- All three new regression tests fail on the original schemas because arc bulges are stripped, and pass with this change.
- `bun test`: 546 passed, covering rounded board corners, clockwise circular cutouts, and a major arc followed by a straight slot segment.
- Type checking, ESM/declaration build, Zod lint, snake-case checks, and Biome checks on changed files pass.

title: RFC: store per-net PCB trace clearance on source_net
description: Proposes the Circuit JSON contract for per-net PCB trace clearance by storing the authoring value on source_net.min_trace_clearance as an optional finite, nonnegative number in millimeters.
body:
Proposes the Circuit JSON contract for per-net PCB trace clearance. Store the authoring value on `source_net.min_trace_clearance` as an optional finite, nonnegative number in millimeters. Keep the field absent when the author omits it. An explicit zero adds no clearance above the applicable existing minimum.

### Pair rule

Measure the shortest copper-edge-to-copper-edge gap on a shared copper layer between different electrical nets. The rule covers trace–trace, trace–pad, and trace–via copper pairs, including fixed traces and the copper on layers spanned by a via. Use the existing rules for pairs outside that scope.

For each applicable pair, take the maximum of the existing clearance for that pair and the values on both electrical nets. A missing value contributes zero. Use electrical connectivity to identify each net. If multiple `source_net` records resolve to the same electrical net, take the largest declared value across those records. With an existing minimum of 0.10 mm and net minima of 0.15 mm and 0.25 mm, the required gap is 0.25 mm regardless of which side has the trace.

### Downstream contract

- Core copies the parsed `<net minTraceClearance="0.25mm" />` value into this field.
- The autorouter needs the per-net values and matching electrical net IDs for route connections and existing copper, including nets with no pending connections. Checks reads the same requirement from saved Circuit JSON and evaluates the finished copper independently.
- A small integration repro can declare two nets and fixed copper directly in the TSX test body. With the values above, a 0.20 mm gap should flag a clearance violation and the router should find a path with at least 0.25 mm of clearance when room exists.

The schema test covers omission, zero, JSON round-tripping, and rejection of negative, non-finite, and nonnumeric values. Named net classes and class-to-class rules are tracked in [tscircuit#5808](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5808) and [Checks #550](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/550).

[Companion Props proposal](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/1027)

title: Add assembly.sticker props
description: Adds assemblyProps.sticker for an assembly.sticker  element, allowing users to apply adhesive stickers to parts in their assemblies.
body:
Adds `assemblyProps.sticker` for an `<assembly.sticker />` element: an adhesive sticker applied to one surface of its parent part. Props only; core still has to register the element and emit Circuit JSON (proposed in tscircuit/circuit-json#1018).

```tsx
<assembly.printedpart name="LID" jscad={<Lid />}>
  <assembly.sticker
    name="LABEL"
    imageUrl="./label.svg"
    surfaceRef="topSurface"
    width="36mm"
    height="17mm"
  />
</assembly.printedpart>
```

It is a child of `assembly.part` or `assembly.printedpart` and is positioned exactly like a laser engraving, reusing `ManufacturingSurfacePlacementProps`. It sits in the `assembly` namespace and takes BOM props because, unlike an engraving, it is a separate purchased item.

## Accepted inputs, output and defaults

| Prop | Accepted input | Parsed output | Omission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Nonblank string | Trimmed | Rejected |
| `displayName` | String | Unchanged | Absent |
| `imageUrl` | Nonempty URL string or static-file import | String | Absent; an unprinted sticker |
| `width`, `height` | Finite positive mm number or distance string | Number in mm | With `imageUrl`, one may be absent and follows the image's aspect ratio. Without it, both are required |
| `thickness` | Finite positive mm number or distance string | Number in mm | Absent; no thickness is assumed |
| `backgroundColor` | Nonblank string | Trimmed | Absent |
| `surfaceRef`, offsets, edge distances, `anchorAlignment`, `rotationOnSurface` | Same as `manufacturing.laserengraving.*` | Same | `surfaceRef` rejected; `anchorAlignment` defaults to `"center"` |
| `supplierPartNumbers`, `purchaseUrls` | Same as other assembly parts | Same | Absent |

There are no aliases. The change is additive, so nothing migrates; old core versions ignore the element.

## Conflicts

- Two position props on one axis are rejected, as for engravings.
- Giving both `width` and `height` with an `imageUrl` stretches the artwork to that size.

## Open questions

- **Child or sibling.** The laser engraving proposal suggested a sticker might instead be a sibling part attached with `mountedTo`. This PR makes it a child with `surfaceRef` because face mounting has no edge distances or rotation on the surface, and would need a `mountFace` that a sticker does not have.
- **Shape and stock.** Rectangles only. Corner radius, die-cut outlines, material and finish are left out.

title: RFC: add minTraceClearance to net props
description: Proposes the optional minTraceClearance?: Distance prop on net.
body:
Proposes the optional `minTraceClearance?: Distance` prop on `<net>`.

```tsx
<net name="USB_DP" minTraceClearance="0.15mm" />
<net name="RF_SIGNAL" minTraceClearance="0.25mm" />
```

The shared distance parser normalizes numbers in millimeters and unit strings such as `"10mil"` to finite, nonnegative millimeters. Omission leaves the value undefined.

The value applies to the copper-edge gap between a trace and a different net’s trace, pad, or via on a shared layer. The required gap is the largest of the applicable existing minimum and the two nets’ values. Core can copy the parsed value directly to `source_net.min_trace_clearance`.

Tests cover omission, numeric millimeters, unit conversion, zero, and invalid values. The Circuit JSON companion carries the consumer contract and the routing/DRC acceptance case. [Circuit JSON proposal](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/1019)

title: feat: propose manufacturing.laserengraving text and image props
description: Proposes a manufacturing namespace with two elements for laser-engraved marks on a part surface. They are children of assembly.printedpart or assembly.part. Elements are named for the process, so a mark says how it is made and not only how it looks.
body:
Proposes a `manufacturing` namespace with two elements for laser-engraved marks on a part surface. They are children of `assembly.printedpart` or `assembly.part`. Elements are named for the process, so a mark says how it is made and not only how it looks.

```tsx
<assembly.printedpart name="LID" jscad={<Lid />} material="petg">
  <manufacturing.laserengraving.text
    text="REV B"
    surfaceRef="topSurface"
    fontSize="3mm"
    distanceFromSurfaceLeftEdge="4mm"
    distanceFromSurfaceTopEdge="4mm"
  />
  <manufacturing.laserengraving.image
    imageUrl="./logo.svg"
    surfaceRef="badge"
    width="18mm"
    rotationOnSurface="90deg cw"
  />
</assembly.printedpart>
```

## What's in it

- **Surface.** `surfaceRef` is required: a built-in bounding surface (`topSurface`, `bottomSurface`, `leftSurface`, `rightSurface`, `frontSurface`, `backSurface`) or a named reference surface on the parent part.
- **Position.** At most one prop per axis, in the surface's frame: `xOffsetFromSurfaceCenter`, `distanceFromSurfaceLeftEdge`, `distanceFromSurfaceRightEdge`, and the same three for Y. An axis with none is centered. `anchorAlignment` picks the mark's anchor point. `rotationOnSurface` takes degrees or a string such as `"90deg ccw"` or `"90deg cw"`.
- **Laser engraving.** `engravingDepth` and `resultingColor` on both elements; `text`, `fontSize`, `font`, `textStyle` on text; `imageUrl`, `width`, `height`, `rasterMode`, `invertImage` on image.
- **Registry.** `manufacturingProps.laserengraving.text` and `.image`, mirroring `enclosureProps.fdm.box`.

The full contract (accepted inputs, parsed output, defaults, conflicts, core acceptance cases) is in `docs/proposals/manufacturing-laserengraving.md`.

## Reference surface `outwardNormal`

`assembly.referencesurface` gains `outwardNormal`, the direction a surface faces; a mark is engraved on and seen from that side. `normalDirection` remains as an alias with the same meaning. Giving both with different values is rejected, and parsed output carries both names with the same value, so current core keeps working.

## Shared rotation parser

`rotationOnSurface` uses a new `lib/common/rotation` parser, which now also backs `pcbRotation`, `schRotation`, `schematicrect`'s `rotation` and the KiCad footprint `rotation`.

- **Accepted.** A number in degrees, or `"<n>"`, `"<n>deg"` or `"<n>rad"` with an optional `ccw` or `cw`. Parsed to degrees counterclockwise.
- **Behavior change.** `"90deg cw"` used to parse to `90` because the direction was ignored; it is now `-90`. Strings outside the grammar (for example `"90 degrees"`) and non-finite numbers used to parse leniently or to `NaN`; they are now rejected.
- **Unchanged.** Bend angles, arc angles and source phases keep the circuit-json parser.

Every rotation string in tscircuit/core's lib, tests and docs (`"270deg"`, `"90deg"`, `"-90"`, `"45"` and similar) fits the new grammar.

## Open questions

- **"Top" means +Z here.** Board edges use `topedge` for +Y and the face-mounting proposal calls +Y "top" and +Z "above". The alternative is `aboveSurface`/`belowSurface`.
- **Built-in surfaces need part bounds.** Imported models have `modelBounds`, but `jscad` parts are emitted as a plan without evaluating geometry, so core has to evaluate bounds or leave built-in surfaces for the consumer to resolve.
- **Machine settings** (power, speed, pass count) are left out.

## Notes

- Props only. Nothing renders until core supports these elements.
- `generated/PROPS_OVERVIEW.md` also picks up `PcbDriverReceiverChannelProps` and `SimulationEyeDiagramProps`, which were missing from the generated file on main.

On this SEPIC board, requesting either 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm produces identical routing input with minTraceToPadEdgeClearance: 0.1. The larger requested spacing is silently lost before routing, so changing this setting does not enforce the intended clearance. This reproduction renders the full board TSX, retains its manual traces, and captures the input passed to the native local autorouter. Type check and production build pass. Source fixture retains the boards components, placements and eight manual traces; no production code changes.
body:
### Motivation

Increasing `autorouter.traceClearance` should change the clearance requested from the router. On this SEPIC board, requesting either 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm produces identical routing input with `minTraceToPadEdgeClearance: 0.1`. The larger requested spacing is silently lost before routing, so changing this setting does not enforce the intended clearance.

This reproduction renders the full board TSX, retains its manual traces, and captures the input passed to the native local autorouter. The passing characterization test records the current bug; each snapshot labels the requested clearance and the received input field. Those labels describe routing settings, not measured copper gaps.

| Requested: 0.25 mm | Requested: 0.50 mm |
| --- | --- |
| ![Board requesting 0.25 mm; router receives 0.1 mm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/core/5c476f43e2f901dc405c4708c5549ecfa778dd05/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-autorouter-clearance-board-0.25mm-pcb.snap.svg) | ![Board requesting 0.50 mm; router receives 0.1 mm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/core/5c476f43e2f901dc405c4708c5549ecfa778dd05/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-autorouter-clearance-board-0.50mm-pcb.snap.svg) |

### Validation

- Reproduction and snapshot verification pass: 1 test, 7 assertions.
- Type check and production build pass.
- Source fixture retains the board's components, placements and eight manual traces; no production code changes.

title: chore: bump autorouter to 0.0.1128 and fanout solver to 0.0.86
description: Updates the autorouter and fanout solver dependencies to their latest versions, ensuring compatibility and improved functionality in routing and clearance checks.
body:
Bump `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` to `^0.0.1128` for tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3939, which checks direct and inset routes against neighboring pads and removes the captured A13 BALL_C3 contact. Bump `@tscircuit/fanout-solver` from main’s `0.0.85` to `0.0.86` for tscircuit/fanout-solver#290, allowing through-vias across reserved inner-layer pours while protecting terminal-layer pours and foreign copper. Both npm releases and their merged source contents are verified. Bus-lanes-solver is current at `0.0.62`.

The A13 D0–D3 fixture is a negative case for the configured **0.2 mm** clearance. Its known DRAM_D3 finding moves from U200.BALL_F9 (0.088046 mm) to U200.BALL_E9 (0.078536 mm). Remove the incidental 0.08 mm bounds on previously observed failing output; they were introduced to characterize that output, and are not board design rules. Keep the bounded known 0.2 mm violations, connectivity, no drilled pads, and all other physical checks. Explicitly reject trace/pad and via/pad overlap with zero-clearance checks. The separate eighteen-path A13 fixture still requires zero DRC findings at 0.2 mm.

Refresh affected routing snapshots, including A13, RP2040 saved-path replay, INA237 pin attribution, Watchy, and the regulator breakout. Resolve main’s fanout-version conflict by preserving `0.0.86` and core’s current version.

Validation:
- Autorouter npm SHA-1/SHA-512, merged ancestry, bundled source maps, and fresh Bun/Node workers verified; native build and 20 native tests passed (484 assertions).
- Fanout npm hashes, ancestry, and all 95 published source files verified; 7 native tests passed (145 assertions), including the new plane-drop clearance regression.
- Core focused regression suite and fanout integrations passed; after conflict resolution and removing incidental bounds, 7 targeted tests passed (101 assertions) without snapshot-update mode.
- The repository’s focused Ubuntu snapshot-update action regenerated the two A13 snapshots; both tests passed with their physical/connectivity assertions intact. Before/after images inspected. All ten Bun test shards, typecheck, formatting, class exports, distribution smoke test, package preview, and Vercel passed on `0a255c3c6aa2cf2819b4a768bd8248f05b47c5d1` ([Bun Test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/44353731536)).

Remaining A13 clearance violations are explicit in the negative fixture; this update does not claim that fixture meets 0.2 mm clearance.

title: Prevent recursive renders from routing preview reads
description: Fixes recursive rendering issue in routing callbacks that prevents proper copper pours from being generated during autorouting.
body:
Prevent `getCircuitJson()` in a routing callback from starting a recursive render. One guard in `IsolatedCircuit.render()` lets the existing phase dependencies generate copper pours after routed vias exist. `isDoneRendering()` also stays false during an active render. Pours wait for routing to finish.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Vias available to the focused pour | 1 of 2 | 2 of 2 |
| Final H616 connected nets | 2 / 121 | 2 / 121 |

#5657 supplies the `test.failing` repro; this fix enables it as a normal passing test. Core CI: **2,317 passed, zero failures**; type, build, smoke and formatting checks pass. [Source regression](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/44261599517) · [H616 run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/44262644185).

title: Keep small-board mouse bites drillable (#5066)
description: Adjusts mouse-bite drill sizes for small boards to ensure they remain drillable according to JLCPCBs specifications, while addressing clearance issues with traces.
body:
**Stack:** 2/2, #5492, the repro → this fix. Merge #5658 first, then merge this into the repro branch, then merge #5492 (now containing the fix) to `main`.

**Depends on #5658**, which bumps `@tscircuit/jlcpcb-manufacturing-specs` to the release with `jlcPanelRules`. This branch includes that bump, so `package.json` shows it here until #5658 merges.

**JLCPCB rules:** the minimums now come from `jlcPanelRules` instead of hardcoded numbers:
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_DIAMETER` = `jlcPanelRules.min_non_plated_hole_diameter` (0.5 mm, JLCPCB's minimum non-plated hole)
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_SPACING` = `jlcPanelRules.recommended_mouse_bite_spacing.max` (0.3 mm, the stronger end of JLCPCB's recommended 0.2–0.3 mm)

The values are unchanged, so no snapshots move.

Stacked on #5492. Fixes the small-board case of #5066. **Draft for review:** it includes a tradeoff, described below.

Tabs shrink on small boards, and the mouse-bite drills used to shrink with them, down to 0.27 mm drills at a 0.405 mm pitch. `getMouseBiteSize` in `lib/utils/panels/generate-panel-tabs-and-mouse-bites.ts` now has two named minimums:
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_DIAMETER`: a 0.5 mm drill
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_SPACING`: a 0.3 mm web between holes

That gives a 0.8 mm pitch on small boards, the "about 0.5 mm holes at about 0.8 mm pitch" asked for in the issue. Boards whose scaled drill is already above the minimums don't change. The issue's 14 × 18 mm example keeps 0.63 mm drills at a 0.945 mm pitch.

**Repro.** The test is unchanged. In its snapshots, the first two drills go from 0.27 mm at a 0.405 mm pitch to 0.5 mm at a 0.8 mm pitch. Each tab now has one row of drills on the board edge. The second row on the far side of the 0.6 mm slot is dropped, because it would sit closer than the minimum pitch to the first row.

**Other snapshots updated by the larger drills:**
- `panel-with-tabs` (custom props)
- `panel-traces-routing-bounds`
- `subpanel13`
- `repro80-tab-routing-too-big` (both snapshots)

**Tradeoff to review: repro86.** Its boards are only 2 mm tall. A 0.5 mm drill centred on the board edge now comes within 0.166 mm of the R1–R2 trace, and the required clearance is 0.2 mm. The test used to assert zero errors. It now expects 32 `pcb_trace_error`s and snapshots the message. The issue asked for exactly this: holes kept clear of copper, "or at least a warning". Alternatives, if you'd rather avoid the errors:
- Move the drills outward so they reach less far into the board.
- Allow drills below 0.5 mm on very small tabs.

All 123 panel tests and the typecheck pass locally.

Other open PRs for #5066: #5262, and the #5463 → #5464 stack.

title: fix: round-trip branched saved routing phases
description: Fixes saved-phase failures by ensuring complete phases validate copper connectivity for export and replay, allowing shared anchor pads and junctions while rejecting cross-net connections.
body:
Fixes the saved-phase failures reproduced in #5643. Complete phases now use physical copper connectivity to validate both export and replay. A path can share an anchor pad or meet another path at a same-layer junction. Each requested connection still has to be covered, and copper that joins different electrical nets is rejected.

Export keeps the solver’s route order and chooses a port from the connected copper as the frame for `pcbTracePaths`. Replay resolves ownership before inserting the copper. A saved phase can claim an implicit same-net connection when its copper joins the endpoints, leaving uncovered connections for later routing.

The four inline repros now check successful replay. The default-router case saves and replays the same routes. Two focused tests cover phase ownership through a plated pad and cross-net rejection. The existing saved fanout tests exercise the separate escape and handoff behavior.

This builds on the coverage in #5614 and targets the merged repros on `main`.

title: test: add inline TSX repros for saved routing phases
description: Adds four small TSX reproductions for the saved-phase bug in 5614, providing tests for various routing scenarios that previously resulted in errors during autorouting.
body:
Adds four small TSX reproductions for the saved-phase bug in #5614. Each test contains the whole board, uses three or four test points, and has a PCB snapshot. The replay examples put the literal paths on `<autoroutingphase pcbTracePaths={...} />`.

- **Save across connections.** The default autorouter routes logical A–B and B–C connections through pad C. Both traces are present on the PCB, but the phase event has no saved paths.
- **Shared pad.** Saved A–B and A–C paths both start at A. Replay reports a duplicate path and emits zero traces.
- **T-junction.** A saved path from C touches the middle of the A–B trace. Replay requires another pad at the end and emits zero traces.
- **Trunk.** An internal segment joins the middle of A–B to the middle of C–D. Replay requires the trunk to start at a pad and emits zero traces.

All four tests reproduce the current behavior on `main`. On #5614, the three replay boards restored two, two, and three traces with no autorouting errors. The export board produced two saved paths, and replaying them preserved the coordinates, widths, and layers of the original copper.

This is a standalone reproduction PR for the cases discussed in #5613.

title: fix(pcb): exclude system diagram geometry from SVG bounds

body:

title: chore: bump schematic placement analysis to v0.0.98
description: Bumps tscircuitcircuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis to v0.0.98, removing false inverted rails warnings for specific components in the schematic.
body:
Bumps `@tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis` from `27e166a` (v0.0.97) to `45604fe` (v0.0.98).

v0.0.98 includes tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis#464, which only reports `TwoPinComponentHasInvertedRails` for parts between a positive supply and ground. On the TI TPS25751EVM fixture from #578, this removes 13 false `inverted_rails` warnings on pull-up resistors from signal lines to 3V3 (R13–R18, R48–R53, R117).

### Test updates
Two tests asserted the old behavior and now expect no warning:
- `check-schematic-placement-pull-resistors.test.tsx`: a pull-up with its supply pin facing down is no longer reported as inverted rails.
- `check-schematic-placement-inverted-ground.test.tsx`: a capacitor between ground and a signal net, ground facing up, is no longer reported.

title: Reuse the rendered Drawing view when switching package tabs
description: Reduces model download time by reusing the rendered Drawing view when switching tabs, preventing unnecessary model downloads and improving performance.
body:
Returning to Drawing currently starts another model download and render, which took about 37 seconds for Classic F1 in a profiled browser run. The PCB and 3D tabs already preserve their expensive viewers between tab changes.

Use that same KeepMountedView mechanism for Drawing. It mounts on first use and retains the rendered sheet and loaded model URLs when another tab is active. Its existing release/build identity pattern resets the viewer when either changes.

Stacked on #6008. This fix removes the expected-failure marker and changes the return-to-Drawing snapshot from a loading message to the completed sheet. The test stalls subsequent model downloads, verifies the original image remains connected, and checks that no additional models were requested. The second regression verifies lazy loading and selected-build invalidation.

This is an in-page cache implemented with the existing viewer lifecycle. It requires no new DrawingViewer prop, global cache, dependency bump, or additional Classic F1 build.

A local browser check also used the full published Classic F1 circuit (3,570 elements) and all 27 unique model files. Returning to Drawing took 312 ms, retained the original image element, and made zero additional model requests, with further model downloads blocked.

Validation:

- `bunx playwright test playwright-tests/package-drawing-cache1.spec.ts playwright-tests/package-drawing-cache2.spec.ts playwright-tests/package-drawing-view.spec.ts --retries=0 --workers=1` — all 6 tests passed, including desktop and mobile navigation.
- `bun test` — 430 passed, 5 existing skips.
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run lint`

![Returning to the cached Drawing view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/codex/drawing-tab-cache-fix/playwright-tests/snapshots/package-drawing-cache1.spec.ts-classic-f1-return-to-drawing.png)

title: test: reproduce Classic F1 drawing regeneration between tabs
description: Reproduces a bug where returning to the Drawing tab unmounts the existing DrawingViewer and causes unnecessary model downloads, impacting performance.
body:
Returning to Drawing after opening another tab unmounts the existing DrawingViewer, disposes its model URLs, and starts the drawing over. On the live Classic F1 page, returning to the tab took about 37 seconds in a profiled browser run.

This repro uses the existing Classic F1 service-sheet fixture and its relative LCD OBJ. After the first drawing appears, the test stalls further LCD downloads and switches Files → Drawing. The snapshot records the actual Loading engineering drawing state. The regression then checks that the original image is still connected, the drawing is visible, and no models were downloaded again.

The website uses Playwright, so its native `test.fail()` is the equivalent of Bun’s `test.failing`. The marker is set after the snapshot check, so a broken snapshot cannot satisfy the expected failure. Removing the marker was verified to fail specifically because the original drawing image was detached.

A separate passing browser test verifies that Drawing is not loaded before its first use and that selecting another build discards the previous drawing. Its second build exists only in the test fixture; Classic F1’s published single build is unchanged.

Validation:

- `bunx playwright test playwright-tests/package-drawing-cache1.spec.ts playwright-tests/package-drawing-cache2.spec.ts`

![Actual return to Drawing before the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/codex/drawing-tab-cache-repro/playwright-tests/snapshots/package-drawing-cache1.spec.ts-classic-f1-return-to-drawing.png)

description: Adds a Drawing tab to the package page for inspecting engineering drawings alongside PCB, schematic, and 3D views.
body:

Stacked on #5961, which reproduces the `#drawing` fallback to Files. This fix removes the expected-failure marker and updates the screenshot to show the Drawing tab and its three-view sheet. The browser test also checks the LCD file request. Uses the published `@tscircuit/drawing-viewer` version `0.0.7`, which includes the model lookup fix and `circuit-json-to-gltf` version `0.0.166`.

title: Use the text index to narrow searches by package
description: Optimizes search functionality by incorporating package codes into the text index, reducing candidate results and improving search speed.
body:
A search for `resistor` with `package=0805` currently finds resistors in every package before checking which ones are `0805`. This PR gives the text index the package code too, so D1 can start with fewer candidates. D1 still checks the exact package and orders results by stock. If the search already includes the package code, the index only checks it once.

On a synthetic 150,000-part SQLite catalog, that example went from 85,715 to 25,221 index candidates and from 33 ms to 23 ms median with identical top 100 results.

Validated with 649 repository tests, 100 local Worker tests, TypeScript, and formatting.

title: fix: include LED Indication - Discrete subcategory in led derived table
description: Adds LED Indication - Discrete to ledTableSpec.listCandidateComponents so standard indicator LEDs are included in the led derived table and ledslist, while updating metadata parsing for discrete indicator LEDs.
body:
Adds `"LED Indication - Discrete"` to `ledTableSpec.listCandidateComponents` so standard indicator LEDs (such as basic 0603/0805 parts C2286, C2290, C84256, and C2297) are included in the `led` derived table and `/leds/list`.

Also updates `ledTableSpec.mapToTable` for discrete indicator LED metadata:
- Safely parses optional or missing `extra` JSON so rows without `extra.attributes` are retained and populated from description fallbacks.
- Supports alternate JLCPCB attribute names (`Illumination Color`, `Voltage - Forward(Vf)`, `Test Current`, `Wavelength - Dominant`, `Power(Watts)`, `Mounting Style`) and value ranges (e.g. `1.8V~2.4V`).
- Prevents `<color> lens` descriptors (e.g. `White Yellow Lens`) and `light`/`emerald` modifiers from polluting emitted `color`.

Fixes #650

title: Fix CLI startup with current Circuit JSON schemas
description: Fixes CLI startup failure when using Circuit JSON 0.0.552 due to removed schemas in the bundled PCB SPICE pipeline, by updating to the renamed signal-integrity-pipeline and adjusting imports accordingly.
body:
Installing the CLI alongside Circuit JSON 0.0.552 makes `tsci init -y` fail before command execution: the bundled PCB SPICE pipeline 0.1.8 statically imports the removed simulation_ibis_pin_state and simulation_digital_stimulus schemas.

Replace the old package with the renamed @tscircuit/signal-integrity-pipeline 0.1.11 release and update simulation imports, type imports, and the native timeout fixture. Its public pipeline and adapter entry points remain compatible and it resolves record schemas through the Circuit JSON namespace.

Add a regression that bundles the CLI simulation entry point with those superseded schemas unavailable. It fails against 0.1.8 with both missing-export errors and passes against 0.1.11. All five Linux test shards, Windows tests, type checking, TypeScript 5/7 compatibility, dependency ownership on both platforms, compiled CLI smoke tests, PCB style checks, formatting, and the real return-current EM simulation passed. The new regression and existing native solver timeout tests passed in CI. One runner stalled for 11 minutes installing FFmpeg; its shard was retried on a fresh runner and passed.

Unblocks tscircuit/tscircuit#6500.

title: Avoid direct high-density shortcuts through neighboring pads
description: Validates all direct shortcuts and inset candidates against existing point and segment collision checks to prevent routing through neighboring pads, improving routing accuracy and reducing copper shorts.
body:
A13’s direct routing shortcut clips neighboring RAM pad BALL_C3.

Validate every direct shortcut and inset candidate with the existing point and segment collision checks. Reject blocked candidates and continue the normal search. Share pad geometry checks with TraceWidthSolver, and include pad geometry in the route cache.

| A13 result | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Full TSX/Core: signals connected | 96/96 | 96/96 |
| Full TSX/Core: actual copper shorts | 2 | 1 |
| Full TSX/Core: total DRC findings | 13 | 13 |
| Captured declared-clearance snapshot: DRC findings | 9 | 7 |
| Captured fixed-copper snapshot: DRC findings | 8 | 7 |

The contact is removed; insufficient-clearance findings remain.

The two snapshot checks use the same captured A13 board.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![RAM pad contact](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/7a0ff8fd4f44b905d13bea75c50bfa3cb8d6ba0e/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-a13-regional-repair-shorts-copper-contacts.snap.svg) | ![Contact removed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/f68a180c3820ad0c73b1a9207bb2ced33211d860/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-a13-regional-repair-shorts-copper-contacts.snap.svg) |

Stacked on #3917.

<details>
<summary>Benchmarks and DDR progress</summary>

Prepare nearby pads once per region and share them between routing candidates. Memoize each fixed pad list’s geometry digest for cache keys. Skip pad-check calls when the constructor has disabled that context; all pad collision rules remain enabled.

Two paired comparisons on 8-vCPU ARM runners, with identical dependencies and three sample workers per pair. The second pair reverses the execution order. Times below average the two runs per revision; combined times sum all 16 samples.

| Dataset18 | Before optimization | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P50 sample time | 27.69 s | 27.64 s | -0.2% |
| P95 sample time | 100.02 s | 97.93 s | -2.1% |
| Combined sample time | 615.2 s | 608.4 s | -1.1% |
| High-density time | 279.1 s | 272.8 s | -2.2% |
| Solved and DRC-clean | 16/16 | 16/16 | unchanged |
| Total vias | 3,396 | 3,396 | unchanged |

All 16 samples produce identical copper across all four passes. The individual paired total-time changes are +0.2% and -2.4%, so this is a modest improvement.

The A13 SVG snapshots and routing assertions pass unchanged, along with the focused collision tests, types, and existing Game Boy/H616 regressions.

[Paired dataset18 comparisons and A13/build checks](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/44338768531)

The existing full-board tradeoffs remain: ButterStick uses six additional vias, and the legacy NEMA snapshot has one additional spacing finding (0.094 mm against a 0.1 mm rule; total findings 13 → 14).

| Board | Initial recorded result | Latest verified progress |
|---|---|---|
| OrangeCrab | 50/50 connected | 50/50, zero physical findings |
| H3 | 0/53 exported | 16/53; 37 remain unrouted |
| A64 | 0/75 exported | 32/75; 43 remain unrouted |
| STM32MP157 | 0/72 exported | 32/72; 40 remain unrouted |
| A13 | 0/96 exported | 96/96; 1 actual short, 13 total findings with this PR |
| H616 | 0/53 exported | 53/53, zero physical findings |
| ButterStick | 0/55 exported | 55/55, zero physical findings |
| Glider | 49/49 connected | 49/49, zero physical findings |
| i.MX6 | 53/53 connected | 53/53, zero physical findings |
| iCE/Pi | 0/50 exported | 50/50, zero physical findings |

Initial observations: #3757. Published baseline: tscircuit 0.0.3230, Core 0.0.2408, autorouter 0.0.1123, bus-lanes-solver 0.0.61. The comparison overrides only the autorouter.
</details>

title: repro: BGA escape ignores its existing via-in-pad
description: Fixes the issue where the BGA escape routing adds an additional via beside an existing via-in-pad instead of utilizing the existing via, leading to unnecessary complexity in the routing.
body:
The 6×6 BGA fixture from [core#5673](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5673) already has a 0.45 mm via drilled into U1.pin15. title: Resolve selected CAD model URLs at load time
description: Allows the glTF converter to resolve CAD model URLs at load time, preventing missing models in the 3D scene by utilizing a shared lookup function from the website.
body:
Classic F1 stores its LCD model at `./mechanical/cad/lcd-module.obj` inside its published package. Loading that path relative to the website page can return HTML, leaving the LCD missing from the 3D scene and engineering drawing.

The website already knows which package release contains the file. This PR lets it share that lookup with the glTF converter through an optional `resolveStaticAsset(modelUrl)` function.

After choosing a model to load, the converter calls this function to get a usable URL, then loads the model through the existing OBJ, STL, GLB, glTF, or STEP loader. DrawingViewer can pass through the website's existing lookup, removing the need for the website to copy Circuit JSON and rewrite its model paths.

Stacked on #297, which reproduces the missing LCD using Classic F1's relative file path and a PNG snapshot. This fix changes `test.failing` to a regular test and updates the snapshot to show the LCD above the PCB.

Validation completed with these commands.

- `bun test tests/snapshot/classic-f1-relative-model.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Skip shading for constant unlit opaque surfaces
description: Optimizes rendering by skipping shading calculations for constant unlit opaque surfaces, reducing computational load and improving performance without altering visual output.
body:
Classic F1’s outline drawing spends time calculating normals and interpolating shader attributes even though its surfaces are a constant opaque white. This keeps the browser busy without changing the resulting drawing.

Compute the display color once for constant unlit opaque materials, skip unused normal and vertex shading work, and keep the existing clipping and depth tests. Textured, emissive, transparent, masked, and realistically lit materials retain their existing rendering paths. No public options are added.

Stacked on #57. This fix removes `test.failing` and updates the actual-render snapshot’s interpolation count from 419,382 to zero. The drawing region itself is byte-for-byte identical to the repro snapshot. The independent material comparison also remains pixel-identical.

Local timing comparison for the same three-view fixture, after one warmup and with three measured samples: P50 5.335 s → 4.815 s, P95 5.460 s → 5.426 s. This benchmark excludes model downloads. Browser timing will depend on the machine and drawing size; the website cache is a separate stack that avoids rendering again when switching tabs.

A separate one-pass check at Classic F1’s viewport sizes (560×488, 488×256, and 872×896, with 2× supersampling) took 17.724 s before and 7.528 s after. All three RGBA buffers were byte-for-byte identical. This check measures rasterization of the fixture’s top, front, and isometric views; it excludes downloads and scene construction.

Validation:

- `bun test` — 93 passing tests across 43 files.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun scripts/benchmark-classic-f1-outline.ts`

title: test: reproduce redundant Classic F1 outline shading

Classic F1’s engineering drawing renders constant white surfaces, but the software renderer still computes surface normals and interpolates vertex colors and normals for every visible pixel. This adds CPU work and allocations while the browser waits for the drawing.

This repro uses the original assembled GLB from desk-fidget-counter v6.0.12, compressed with gzip without simplifying its geometry. Its 81 draw calls contain 374,382 triangles. The test renders top, front, and isometric outlines and records 419,382 shader interpolations where none are needed.

The `test.failing` assertion expects zero interpolations. Setup and PNG snapshot checks run in `beforeAll`, outside the expected failure. The snapshot shows the actual board and measured interpolation count. A separate passing visual test compares constant materials against an interpolated reference, covering output gamma, opaque and masked surfaces, transparency, and emission.

The benchmark runs a warmup and three measured samples without network access. Its timings are reported separately from the deterministic regression assertion.

title: feat: add a via-only per-region area fraction to the region cost
description: Adds an optional per-region viaAreaFraction to the region cost, for regions where vias fit in only part of the area.
body:
Adds an optional per-region `viaAreaFraction` to the region cost, for regions where vias fit in only part of the area.

- Serialized regions can set `d.viaAreaFraction` in (0, 1]; it loads into `topology.regionViaAreaFraction`. Missing means 1, so existing graphs are unchanged. Other values throw.
- Only the via term divides by `area * viaAreaFraction`. Trace density and geometry keep the full region.
- Both cost paths use it (`computeRegionCostForRegion` and `DenseRoutingWorkspace`), as does the polygon override.

The autorouter uses it in tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3906 (https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3906), which used to shrink width and height to get the same via price and so also inflated trace density. #3906 now sends `viaAreaFraction` instead and pins this PR's commit (705012a); it needs a re-pin once this merges. With it, A13 via-pad findings go 3 → 1 and H616 is unchanged.

Tests: `region-via-area-fraction-cost` (fraction 0.1 makes only the via term 10x larger) and `region-via-area-fraction-load` (loads the field, rejects 0). The full suite passes (173), along with format and typecheck.

title: fix: only report inverted rails between positive supply and ground
description: Restricts inversion warnings to components with a positive-supply terminal below its ground terminal, removing false positives from valid layouts.
body:
Stacked on #463.

`TwoPinComponentHasInvertedRails` currently flags valid TI layouts when only one terminal is connected to a rail. Restrict the warning to a component whose explicitly positive-supply terminal is below its ground terminal.

- Positive supply ↔ ground: retain the inversion check.
- Positive supply ↔ signal: accept either vertical direction.
- Signal ↔ ground: accept either vertical direction.
- Unknown polarity or conflicting power/ground metadata: keep skipping inversion warnings.

The change removes the supply-to-signal resistor branch and the signal-to-ground passive branch. It uses the existing typed metadata and connectivity, adds no Circuit JSON properties or name-based exceptions, and leaves the horizontal-orientation rule unchanged.

The two TI repro fixtures are unchanged; their expected findings become zero. Existing regressions and their analysis snapshots are updated to remove the same false positives. The Allwinner fixture still reports all 47 positive-supply-to-ground inversions, while its 20 single-rail warnings disappear.

**TI references — cropped to the relevant components**

**1. Positive supply ↔ ground: keep the inversion check.** C3–C7 have `730_VBUS` above and GND below. Reversing these terminals still warns when the supply is explicitly identified as positive.

![TI TPS25751EVM: C3–C7 with the positive supply above and ground below](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d79acf5-7376-4663-9ccf-cf7b7770b3e6)

Source: [TI TPS25751EVM user's guide, SLVUCP9B, Figure 5-1, page 39](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=39).

**2. Positive supply ↔ signal: accept either vertical direction.** R13–R18 have their signal terminals above and the shared `730_LDO_3V3` supply below. This is the pull-up bank reproduced in #463.

![TI TPS25751EVM: R13–R18 signal terminals above the shared positive supply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d59c542c-2421-4141-a67d-1b3b2a656091)

Source: [TI TPS25751EVM user's guide, SLVUCP9B, Figure 5-1, page 39](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=39).

**3. Signal ↔ ground: accept either vertical direction.** R26 (60.4 Ω) has GND above its signal terminal; R25 (60.4 Ω) has GND below. Both are input terminations. This is the exact circuit used by the second repro in #463.

![TI THS4541RGT EVM: R26 with ground above its signal terminal and R25 with ground below](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85feea51-0697-4ef8-9cc6-005186e8142c)

Source: [TI THS4541RGT EVM user's guide, SLOU392, Figure 1, page 4](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slou392/slou392.pdf#page=4). [Table 1, item 25, page 9](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slou392/slou392.pdf#page=9) confirms both resistors are populated.

**4. Unknown polarity or conflicting power/ground metadata: skip the inversion warning.** This is an analyzer metadata guard, not a physical layout arrangement, so it has no TI schematic crop. Terminal height alone cannot establish an inversion without reliable positive-supply and ground classification.

Validation:
- `bun test`: 341 passed; two unchanged Stride tests hit the existing 5-second timeout and both passed separately on rerun (3.53s and 3.50s). No timeout changes.
- `bun run typecheck` passes.
- The complete seven-sheet TPS25751EVM fixture from tscircuit/checks#578 was rendered once and checked with the original and fixed analyzers: 13 warnings → 0, with identical Circuit JSON and no warning filters.
- TI repro snapshots visually inspected; no fixture placement or connectivity changes.

title: Add JLCPCB panelization rules
description: Adds JLCPCBs published panelization rules for PCB manufacturing, including specifications for mouse-bite drills, breakaway tabs, and board spacing.
body:
Adds `jlcPanelRules`: JLCPCB's published panelization rules, in mm, from https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities (the page this package already cites).

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| `min_non_plated_hole_diameter` (mouse-bite drills are non-plated) | 0.5 |
| `recommended_mouse_bite_diameter` | 0.5–0.8 |
| `recommended_mouse_bite_spacing` | 0.2–0.3 |
| `min_breakaway_tab_width` | 4 |
| `min_mouse_bite_breakaway_tab_width` | 5 |
| `panel_board_spacing_options` | 1.6, 2 |
| `min_panel_board_spacing_with_space` | 2 |
| `min_tooling_edge_width` | 3 |
| `min_tooling_edge_width_for_smt_assembly` | 5 |

- **New file:** `lib/jlcpcb-panel-rules.ts`, with a typed `JlcPanelRules` interface and the `jlcPanelRules` constant.
- **Export:** added to `index.ts`.
- **Test:** `tests/jlc-panel-rules.test.ts`, an inline snapshot of the values.
- **README:** one line in the exports list.

These rules are kept separate from `jlcMinTolerances`, because those maps are keyed by `PcbBoard` fields and panel rules aren't.

**Why:** tscircuit/core can use these instead of hardcoded panel constants, for example the small-board mouse-bite minimums in tscircuit/core#5502. It could also check tab widths against JLCPCB's 5 mm minimum.

Locally, the typecheck passes, `bun run format:check` passes and `bun test` gives 7 pass, 0 fail.

title: ci: run bun test as 6 parallel shards balanced by recorded timings
description: This PR modifies the CI workflow to run tests in parallel across 6 shards based on recorded timings, significantly reducing the total test execution time from 55 minutes to approximately 13.5 minutes for the critical path.
body:
The `test` workflow ran every test file in one job, so each PR waited ~55 min. This PR splits it into a 6-job matrix, using the same approach as `tscircuit-autorouter`'s `bun-test.yml`.

## How it works
- `scripts/generate-balanced-test-plan.ts` (ported from the autorouter) reads `test-timings.json` and spreads the test files across shards with longest-first greedy bin packing, writing `.bun-test-plan/testplans/testplanN.txt`. A new file with no recorded timing is costed at the p90.
- `scripts/record-test-timings.ts` rebuilds `test-timings.json` from the per-file `##[group]` markers in a CI run's logs: `bun scripts/record-test-timings.ts <run-id> [...]`.
- `test-timings.json` was seeded from two green `main` runs (44086963002, 44042446919). It covers all 237 files, 55.7 min in total.
- Each shard runs `bun test <files> --timeout 120000`, the same flags as before.
- Superseded PR runs are now cancelled (`main` runs are not), and snapshot diffs are uploaded when a shard fails.
- `test-timings.json` is excluded from the Biome format check because it is generated.

## Expected plan (6 shards)
```
testplan1:   1 files, 13.47 min   <- tests/repros/mt8395-core-full-routing.test.ts
testplan2:  24 files,  8.45 min
testplan3:  25 files,  8.45 min
testplan4:  25 files,  8.45 min
testplan5:  24 files,  8.45 min
testplan6: 138 files,  8.45 min
critical path 13.47 min (was ~55 min)
```
I checked locally that the plans cover all 237 test files exactly once, with no duplicates.

`mt8395-core-full-routing` is one test that solves 138 DDR signals, so it sets the floor. Adding more shards would not lower the wall time unless that test is split.

## Benchmark effect
None. This PR only changes CI: no solver, routing, fixture or benchmark-input code is touched, and the same test files run with the same flags. The `AM3352 benchmark (11/11)` Blacksmith workflow is unchanged.

title: Forward the drawing asset resolver to glTF
description: Allows the website to pass the CAD file lookup to DrawingViewer through an optional resolveStaticAsset function, enabling proper rendering of the LCD model in the drawing.
body:
Classic F1’s drawing refers to its LCD model as `./mechanical/cad/lcd-module.obj`. That path belongs to a published package. Loading it relative to the page can leave the LCD missing from the drawing.

The website already knows how to find files in the selected package release. This PR lets it pass that lookup to DrawingViewer through an optional `resolveStaticAsset` function. DrawingViewer forwards the function to glTF when creating the assembled and exploded views, so the model loader receives a usable file address. It renders again when the lookup changes.

This lets the website use its existing CAD file lookup and remove the workaround that rewrites model paths in Circuit JSON.

Stacked on #15, which reproduces the missing LCD with `test.failing` and an SVG snapshot. This fix makes the test pass and updates the snapshot to show the LCD. Uses the published `circuit-json-to-gltf` version `0.0.166`, which includes tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#298.

title: Kit packaging: UV-laser engraved base, UPC sticker, carton labels, smooth camera, Cosmos order
description: Brings the full-kit line up to its real packaging process, smooths the camera, and lists the main simulation first in Cosmos. Replaces tscircuitmanufacturing-simulation9.
body:
Brings the full-kit line up to its real packaging process, smooths the camera, and lists the main simulation first in Cosmos. Replaces tscircuit/manufacturing-simulation#9.

## Kit boxes: UV laser and UPC sticker

- **New UV laser bench** on the east wall, next to the 3D printers and the label printer: a [ComMarker Omni X](https://store.commarker.com/products/omni-x-uv-laser-engraver) with the slide extension.
  - It engraves "Made in China" on the **base** of 4 blank mailers per run. The boxes lie upside down, 2 across and 2 deep, on the 250 × 400 mm slide.
  - A run takes 20 s of framing plus 12 s per box.
  - The operator unloads a finished run, loads and starts the next, and carries the engraved boxes to the pack-out stacks, the same way plates go from the printers.
  - The shift starts with 12 engraved boxes at pack-out, a finished run on the slide, and the rest blank.
  - The batch run fits laser trips in between benches, and waits for the last run before pack-out if needed.
  - In game mode, press E at the laser bench or on its circle. The control panel has **Engraving done** and **Engrave boxes, take them to pack-out**.
- **Pack-out:**
  - A MUNBYN thermal printer prints the 2 × 1" UPC-A sticker (884400898623, from `tscircuit/product-packaging`).
  - The operator tips the box over and puts the sticker on a corner of the base, beside the engraving and about 8 mm from both edges.
  - Pack-out stops with a message if a unit's box hasn't been engraved yet.
- The bare-unit line has neither the laser nor the UPC printer.

## Carton labels

- The label printer prints the FBA box ID and then a 4 × 6" DHL carrier label. The DHL label is a marked sample showing ship-from, ship-to the fulfillment center, the FBA shipment ID as reference, piece count, weight and tracking bars.
- Both are carried to ship-ready and applied so the carrier label never covers the box ID:
  - **Kit carton:** side by side on the front.
  - **Bag carton (10 × 8 × 6"):** the carrier label goes on the back, because the front can't fit both.
- Cartons get a `carrierLabelSpot`. The label printer holds its sheets while either carton label is printing.

## Camera and scenarios

- The camera's target, distance and angles move on critically damped springs, so a close-up change glides there instead of cutting:
  - Each move starts from rest and settles without overshoot.
  - Long bench-to-bench moves pull back a little on the way.
  - Dragging to orbit takes over at once.
- Removes the "Walk the floor" and "Pick up the screwdriver" scenarios and the patrol route. The F key still picks up the screwdriver in game mode.

## Cosmos order (from tscircuit/manufacturing-simulation#9)

- Renames `pages/bare-unit-bagging.page.tsx` to `pages/manufacturing-simulation-bare-unit.page.tsx`, so Cosmos lists it after the main simulation.
- Moves the README's bare-unit section after the main line's sections.

## Docs

- New `docs/kit-packaging.md` covers the unit-box marks, the carton labels, and the laser model and capacity.
- The README and `docs/bare-unit-packaging.md` are updated.

## Checks

- biome, format check and `tsc` are clean.
- `bun test` passes (40). New tests cover:
  - the laser job and its game action;
  - UPC-A encoding and check digit;
  - a full kit batch with every box engraved and stickered;
  - both carton labels on both cartons;
  - the camera glide and orbit takeover.
- Checked in screenshots: the laser bench and engraving, the UPC sticker going onto the base, the engraved base, and the labels on both cartons.

## Open questions

- **Laser model:** 4 boxes per run assumes the 12 W Omni X with the slide. The 6 W slide fits 2 per run.
- **UPC or FNSKU:** Amazon only accepts the UPC as the unit barcode if the listing uses manufacturer barcodes. Otherwise it needs the FNSKU, with the UPC covered.

body:
A second simulation on the same unit 322 floor: the **bare unit** (no motor), bagged and shipped to Amazon FBA. The full kit line is unchanged.

Open it in Cosmos as `manufacturing-simulation-bare-unit` (listed after the main simulation), or add `?line=bagged` in the vite dev server.

## What's in the bag

The RP2040 board, one 4 mm backface spacer, four long M3 screws in a pink 2"×3" anti-static pouch, and the motor-to-board cable. The parts go in an [Ellbest 80 × 120 mm ESD shielding zip bag](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07QFZBT9Z) with a yellow ESD caution sticker on the back.

## The line

- **No assembly bench.** That table is gone. QC, bagging and ship-ready move up into its place, and the layout drives benches, navigation and parking.
- **QC:** boards wait in a black ESD tray. Each is set on a mat beside the one test motor, never screwed on. The test motor's cable, DATA and PWR are plugged in, the motor is spun, and everything is unplugged. The board goes into the passed tray, which is carried to bagging.
- **Bagging, by hand (no bag holder):**
  1. Fill the screw pouch, zip it and fold it.
  2. Hold the bag open in the left hand. Put in the spacer, the board on top of it, the coiled cable and the pouch, in two piles side by side, then zip.
  3. Lay the bag flat. Put the original tscircuit 2"×4" label on the front, unchanged from `tscircuit/product-packaging`.
  4. Turn the bag over and put the FNSKU label on the back. Then the bag goes into the tote.
- **Ship-ready:** the bags stand on edge in a 10×8×6" carton. The seal step is main's, which prints the 4×6" FBA box ID on the label printer. The label goes on sideways here because the carton is only 6" tall.

## Merge with main

- Uses main's 25-unit `BATCH_SIZE`. The board tray keeps 30 pockets and the bag carton 30 places.
- My earlier pre-placed box ID sticker is gone in favour of main's printed label. Cartons now carry a `boxIdLabelSpot`, which keeps the kit carton's label where it was.
- Keeps main's mobile viewer, with the `productLine` prop added back on top.

title: Add cad_sticker and source_sticker
description: Adds support for cad_sticker and source_sticker elements in Circuit JSON, allowing for the representation of stickers applied to components in circuit assemblies.
body:
Proposes how a sticker appears in Circuit JSON, for the `<assembly.sticker />` element being added in tscircuit/props#1026. Draft for discussion: nothing emits or consumes these records yet apart from the draft renderer in tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#302.

## `cad_sticker`

```json
{
  "type": "cad_sticker",
  "cad_sticker_id": "cad_sticker_0",
  "source_component_id": "source_component_4",
  "applied_to_source_component_id": "source_component_2",
  "center": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 12 },
  "normal_direction": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 1 },
  "x_axis_direction": { "x": 1, "y": 0, "z": 0 },
  "width": 36,
  "height": 17,
  "thickness": 0.15,
  "image_asset": {
    "project_relative_path": "assets/label.svg",
    "url": "https://example.com/assets/label.svg",
    "mimetype": "image/svg+xml"
  },
  "background_color": "#f4f4f2"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `source_component_id` | The sticker's own source component (name, BOM identity) |
| `applied_to_source_component_id` | Optional. The part whose surface carries the sticker; consumers that move that part move the sticker with it |
| `center` | Center of the adhesive face, on the surface. Circuit-world point, mm, +Z above |
| `normal_direction` | Unit direction the printed face points, away from the surface |
| `x_axis_direction` | Unit direction of the artwork's left-to-right, perpendicular to `normal_direction`. Includes any rotation on the surface. The artwork's top is toward `normal_direction × x_axis_direction` |
| `width`, `height` | Required, mm, along `x_axis_direction` and `normal_direction × x_axis_direction` |
| `thickness` | Optional, mm, measured along `normal_direction`. Unspecified when omitted |
| `image_asset` | Optional printed artwork as the shared `Asset` object (SVG or raster), stretched to width by height. Same field name as `pcb_silkscreen_graphic.image_asset` |
| `background_color` | Optional sticker material color, seen where the artwork is transparent or absent |

The frame follows `cad_reference_surface`: the producer resolves the surface, the position on it and the rotation into one world frame, and renderers use it without reapplying the owning part's transform. Parsing rejects non-unit directions and an `x_axis_direction` that is not perpendicular to `normal_direction`. The two direction fields are named `normal_direction` and `x_axis_direction`; `cad_reference_surface` still calls its equivalents `normal` and `x_axis`.

## `source_sticker`

A `source_component` with `ftype: "sticker"`, like `source_printed_part` and `source_motor`. It gives the sticker a name and lets an existing `cad_assembly_bom_item` point at it through `source_component_id`.

## Open questions

- **Owner link.** `applied_to_source_component_id` is how an explosion would carry a sticker with its part. The alternative is making `cad_sticker` an explosion target of its own.
- **Shape.** Rectangles only. Corner radius and die-cut outlines are left out.
- **One element or two.** `cad_sticker` could instead be owned by the part it is applied to and carry its own `name`, as `cad_reference_surface` does, which would drop `source_sticker` but leave the BOM item without a link.

README was not regenerated: `bun run generate-docs` currently rewrites about 280 unrelated lines on main.

title: feat: propose source_laser_engraving_text and cad_laser_engraving_text
description: Proposes how laser-engraved text on an assembly part appears in Circuit JSON, as the counterpart of manufacturing.laserengraving.text  from tscircuitprops1025. It is two records, split the way Circuit JSON already splits source and output: - source_laser_engraving_text: the manufacturing step. What is engraved and how, with no geometry. - cad_laser_engraving_text: the 3D output. Where that text sits on the part, as a resolved world-space frame.
body:
Proposes how laser-engraved text on an assembly part appears in Circuit JSON, as the counterpart of `<manufacturing.laserengraving.text />` from tscircuit/props#1025. It is two records, split the way Circuit JSON already splits source and output:

- **`source_laser_engraving_text`**: the manufacturing step. What is engraved and how, with no geometry.
- **`cad_laser_engraving_text`**: the 3D output. Where that text sits on the part, as a resolved world-space frame.

The props namespace `manufacturing` does not become a Circuit JSON prefix: the step is a `source_` record and its output is a `cad_` record. This is the same pairing as `source_sticker` and `cad_sticker` in #1018.

```json
[
  {
    "type": "source_laser_engraving_text",
    "source_laser_engraving_text_id": "source_laser_engraving_text_0",
    "source_component_id": "source_lid",
    "text": "REV B",
    "engraving_depth": 0.1
  },
  {
    "type": "cad_laser_engraving_text",
    "cad_laser_engraving_text_id": "cad_laser_engraving_text_0",
    "source_laser_engraving_text_id": "source_laser_engraving_text_0",
    "source_component_id": "source_lid",
    "cad_component_id": "cad_component_lid",
    "text": "REV B",
    "font": "tscircuit2024",
    "font_size": 3,
    "anchor_position": { "x": -27, "y": 17, "z": 8 },
    "anchor_alignment": "top_left",
    "normal_direction": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 1 },
    "x_axis_direction": { "x": 1, "y": 0, "z": 0 }
  }
]
```

## Why a cad record

`cad_component` has no texture or image field. A part's appearance comes from its model file, its JSCAD material colors, or the single `color` override, so there is nothing on the part for a mark to attach to. A viewer needs a record that says where the text is.

## Design

- **Source record.** `source_component_id` (the engraved part), `text`, and optional `name` and `engraving_depth`. No default depth.
- **Resolved frame on the cad record.** Like `cad_reference_surface`: `anchor_position` (a point), `normal_direction` (the surface's outward direction) and `x_axis_direction` (the direction the text reads along). The text's up direction is `normal_direction × x_axis_direction`. The producer resolves the surface, edge-relative positioning and rotation.
- **No rotation field.** Rotation on the surface is applied to `x_axis_direction`.
- **Anchor.** `anchor_alignment` refers to the extents of the engraved strokes.
- **Drawn color.** `cad_laser_engraving_text.color`, optional; a renderer derives one from the part when it is omitted.
- **Explosions.** The text moves with its `cad_component_id`. It is not listed in explosion stages or moves.

The full contract is in `docs/proposals/laser-engraving-text.md`. A prototype renderer is in tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#301 (draft), with a snapshot of text on part tops and walls.

## Open questions

- **Where the drawn color lives.** The props `resultingColor` maps to `cad_laser_engraving_text.color`. It could instead sit on the source record as a property of the engraving.
- **A dedicated record or a generic one.** `cad_laser_engraving_text` names the process, as `pcb_silkscreen_text` and `pcb_copper_text` name their layer. The alternative is a process-neutral `cad_surface_text`.
- **Direction names.** This record uses `normal_direction` and `x_axis_direction`. `cad_reference_surface`, which is already released, calls the same two directions `normal` and `x_axis`.
- **README.** The generated element reference in the README is not updated here; regenerating picks up unrelated drift already on main.

## Left out for now

Engraved images, text style, raster settings and curved surfaces.

title: Add cable wires, harness views, drawing tables and balloons
description: Adds new elements for wire harness drawings, including cable wires, harness views, drawing tables, and balloons, enhancing the representation of cable manufacturing in the system.
body:
Elements for wire harness (cable manufacturing) drawings. Rendering is implemented against these in tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing#14; TSX spec in tscircuit/props#1030.

## Cable data

- `cad_cable` gains optional `nominal_length`, `length_tolerance`, `from_connector_name` and `to_connector_name`. `nominal_length` is the manufactured length between the connector wire exits, independent of `path`.
- `cad_cable_wire` (new) is one conductor: `from_pin_number`, `to_pin_number`, and optional `color`, `wire_awg`, `name`. A cavity with no wire is unpopulated, so the two ends of a cable may differ in contact count.

## Drawing records

- `drawing_wiring_harness_view` (new): a flattened view of one `cad_cable` in a paper viewport (`center`, `width`, `height`, like `drawing_part_view`).
- `drawing_table` + `drawing_table_cell` (new): a generic table, modelled on `schematic_table` / `schematic_table_cell`. Cells carry resolved text and inclusive row/column index ranges; they have no geometry of their own, since `column_widths` and `row_heights` determine it.
- `drawing_balloon` (new): a circled callout with one leader to `from_connector`, `to_connector` or `wires` of a harness view. `texts` are resolved by the producer.

`drawing_table` and `drawing_balloon` require both `anchor_position` and a nine-point `anchor_alignment`, so the meaning of a position is always stated in the record.

## Notes for review

- Wires are separate records rather than an array on `cad_cable`, so other elements can reference a wire later.
- The `drawing_wiring_harness_view` description fixes the layout convention: the cable lies flat, so from-end pin 1 is at paper top and to-end pin 1 at paper bottom.
- `cad_cable` still requires both source component ids and a `path`; a cable with no assembly around it is not expressible yet.
- Cross-record checks (pin within its housing, one wire per pin, cells inside their table) are left to consumers, as with the existing drawing elements.
- README docs are not regenerated here: `generate-docs` currently rewrites many unrelated sections.

title: Add wire harness drawing props
description: Add support for wire harness drawings including cable specifications, wiring tables, and BOM tables in TSX format.
body:
TSX spec for wire harness (cable manufacturing) drawings. The cable is described once on `assembly.cable`; the drawing elements only place views of it. Full spec with accepted inputs, parsed outputs and defaults: `docs/proposals/assembly-harness-drawing.md`.

Circuit JSON side: tscircuit/circuit-json#1023.

```tsx
<assembly.cable name="MOTOR_CABLE" from="MOTOR.wireside" to=".CONTROLLER > .J_MOTOR"
  model="adaptercable_a(jst_ph_pins6)_b(jst_ph_pins4)"
  length="50mm" lengthTolerance="3mm"
  fromConnectorName="H1" toConnectorName="H2"
  wireAwg="22awg">
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={1} toPin={1} color="black" />
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={3} toPin={3} color="black" />
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={4} toPin={2} color="black" />
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={6} toPin={4} color="black" />
</assembly.cable>

<assembly.drawing.page size="iso_a4" anchorAlignment="bottom_left">
  <assembly.drawing.harnessview cableRef="MOTOR_CABLE" centerX={148.5} centerY={148}
    width={230} height={76} showBalloons />
  <assembly.drawing.wiringtable cableRef="MOTOR_CABLE" title="Wiring"
    paperX={212} paperY={98} anchorAlignment="top_left" />
  <assembly.drawing.bomtable partRef="MOTOR_CABLE"
    paperX={5} paperY={5} anchorAlignment="bottom_left" />
</assembly.drawing.page>
```

## Changes

- `assembly.cable`: optional `length`, `lengthTolerance`, `fromConnectorName`, `toConnectorName`, `wireAwg`, and `children`. Existing cables parse as before.
- `assembly.cablewire` (new): `fromPin`, `toPin` (a number or a `pinN` label, normalized to a positive integer), and optional `color`, `awg`, `name`.
- `assembly.drawing.harnessview` (new): `cableRef`, the same layout props and conflicts as `partview`, and `showBalloons` (default `false`).
- `assembly.drawing.wiringtable`, `assembly.drawing.bomtable` (new): tables derived from the cable. Both require `paperX`, `paperY` and a nine-point `anchorAlignment`; there is no default position.

## Notes for review

- Circuit JSON has a single generic `drawing_table`. The wiring list and parts list stay separate elements in TSX so the wiring is never retyped by hand; core resolves both into table cells.
- Core emission of these records is not implemented yet.
- The example cable string is currently rejected by cableprinter, which requires both adapter ends to have the same contact count.
- Three existing cable tests switch from a type annotation to `satisfies`, because `length` makes the input type differ from the parsed output.

title: Honor direct solder paste rotation
description: Fixes the issue where a TLV75533PDBVR regulator footprint loses the requested 90 rotation on its stencil apertures, causing misalignment with copper lands.
body:
A TLV75533PDBVR regulator footprint loses the requested 90° rotation on its five explicit stencil apertures. The unrotated openings extend beyond their copper lands and overlap across neighboring pins. This represents the rotated paste-only geometry in Jan Mrázek's item 26, following the merged [Props #1036](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/1036).

Use PrimitiveComponent's existing rotation handling for standalone paste. Reconstruct imported rotated rectangles with their existing angle in `pcbRotation`, so cached geometry follows the same placement path. Remove the separate imported-rotation state and override.

Stacked on [realistic regulator repro #5691](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5691), using published `@tscircuit/props@0.0.741`. The board includes input/output capacitors and real power/ground connections. Its nominal SOT-23-5 land and stencil geometry comes from [TI's DBV0005A examples](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlv755p.pdf#page=38), oriented 90° in the fixture.

Enable the existing regression and update the same PCB snapshot. All five paste openings now align with U1's copper pads.

![The five regulator stencil openings align with their copper lands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/2b5cce70108ab59891006b9a042e78c4facefb83/tests/repros/__snapshots__/paste-direct-rotation-pcb.snap.svg)

title: Reproduce misaligned TLV75533 stencil apertures
description: Reproduces a bug where rotated paste-only apertures cannot be expressed, exposing a rotation bug in the Core.
body:
Jan Mrázek's item 26 reports that rotated paste-only apertures cannot be expressed. [Props #1036](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/1036) is released in `@tscircuit/props@0.0.741`; this repro uses that published version and exposes the remaining Core rotation bug.

Use a TLV75533PDBVR 3.3 V regulator stage with input/output capacitors, VIN/V3V3/GND connections, EN tied to VIN, and NC intentionally unconnected. U1's nominal land and stencil dimensions come from [TI's DBV0005A examples, PDF pages 38–39](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlv755p.pdf#page=38): 1.1 × 0.6 mm openings, 0.95 mm lead pitch, and 2.6 mm between rows. The footprint is oriented 90° from that drawing.

The five U1 copper lands are 0.6 × 1.1 mm. Automatic paste is disabled on those lands so their explicit 1.1 × 0.6 mm apertures can request `pcbRotation={90}`. Core drops that rotation, leaving horizontal openings that extend beyond the copper and overlap across the three adjacent bottom pins. Routing is disabled to isolate stencil generation.

The `test.failing` case checks the actual five emitted U1 apertures after rendering the PCB snapshot. Running it as an ordinary test fails specifically because they remain unrotated rectangles. [Stacked fix #5692](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5692) enables the same test and updates the same snapshot.

![Unrotated paste extends beyond the regulator lands and overlaps adjacent pins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/f85b2be171564796d705ce2f7f16d2471b255391/tests/repros/__snapshots__/paste-direct-rotation-pcb.snap.svg)

The padding solver compares against the nominal 0.2 pin_spacing instead of the drawn pin pitch (0.4 or 0.8, set through schPinStyle margins), and uses a 1e-9 tolerance. body:
Adds the reviewed seven-sheet TI TPS25751EVM schematic under `tests/reference-schematics/`. The test asserts the exact list of schematic warnings the board produces, so any added, removed or changed warning shows up in review. This catches new false positives when schematic checks are added or changed.

The editable TSX contains 261 physical components with native symbols, functional pin labels and pin attributes, automatic trace routing, and the reference section outlines and table borders. The fixture is schematic-only.

Reference: [TI TPS25751EVM User Guide, SLVUCP9B](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf), figures 5-1 through 5-7, pages 39–44. Component placement follows the recreated reference; wire routing is generated by tscircuit.

The test renders all seven sheets, calls `runAllSchematicChecks`, and compares a sorted `sheet component warning-type` summary against the expected list. It then snapshots each sheet as SVG.

Expected warnings (27):
- 13 `schematic_box_too_wide`: all legitimate.
- 14 `schematic_pin_padding_to_edge_too_large`: 6 are legitimate (U1, U4, U6, U7, U8, U11). 8 are known false positives, marked `// FP` in the test (U5, J2–J7, J11). The padding solver compares against the nominal 0.2 `pin_spacing` instead of the drawn pin pitch (0.4 or 0.8, set through `schPinStyle` margins), and uses a 1e-9 tolerance. When the analyzer is fixed, those lines should be removed from the expected list.

The `inverted_rails` warnings from earlier revisions were false positives. They were fixed in the analyzer and are gone since the bump to v0.0.98.

Validation:
- `bun test tests/reference-schematics/tps25751evm.test.tsx` passes (about 10 s locally; the test timeout is 30 s).

body:
The TPS54320 load-step bench can abort before its requested 8 ms stop. Apply TI's supplied PSpice solver profile: 20 ns maximum integration step, ABSTOL=10n, VNTOL=10u, ITL1=1500, ITL2=400 and ITL4=400. Make the default RELTOL=0.001 explicit. Electrical components and load stimulus stay the same.

Report DC regulation over the final 100 µs, alongside peak-to-peak voltage and the final sample. Preserve completed diagnostics when acceptance fails. The unchanged reporting repro naturally updates its text and SVG snapshots. Its recorded 179 mV trace deliberately retains the earlier phase-sensitive reporting case; it is not the corrected profile's output. Stacked on #85. Merge the repro first.

Final 100 µs means are 3.326718 V and 3.327146 V (0.43 mV difference); peak-to-peak voltages are 10.88 mV and 11.25 mV. These final windows are at 0.75 A, whereas TI's measured 10 mV ripple is at 3 A; this is not matched-condition hardware validation. The full power-tree convergence failure remains unresolved.

title: fix: isolate imported SPICE model libraries

title: fix: use the connectivity map for the polyline solver's via lower bound
description: Fixes autorouting failure by utilizing the connectivity map for calculating the via lower bound in the polyline solver, resolving VREF fanout rejection issues.
body:
Alternative to #3968 that fixes the same VREF fanout rejection through the connectivity map instead of a second net-identity mechanism.

`MultiHeadPolyLineIntraNodeSolver` already receives the pipeline's `connMap`, and that map already links each MST branch of a net to its root connection (`getConnectivityMapFromSimpleRouteJson` adds `[connection.name, rootConnectionName]` for every `__rootConnectionNames` entry). The constructor just never consulted it when computing its via lower bound: `getIntraNodeCrossings` counted branches that share a pad as foreign crossings, giving `minViaCount = 6` and the "atleast 6 vias are required" rejection.

The fix is to pass the map to `getIntraNodeCrossings` and skip pairs it connects. The repro now builds the same map the pipeline builds (it previously passed no `connMap`, which the pipeline always does) and routes the fanout.

| C2/C3/R1/R2 VREF fanout | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routed branches | 0/3 | 3/3 |
| Physically connected pads | 0/4 | 4/4 |
| New vias | — | 0 |
| Physical DRC errors | 0 | 0 |

Compared with #3968:

| | #3968 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source of net identity | `rootConnectionName` maps, plus port points rewritten to the `connMap` net id | `connMap` only |
| `lib` changes | 5 files, +145/−18 | 2 files, +10/−2 |
| Routed geometry for the repro | — | identical (both snapshots are byte-identical to #3968's) |
| Existing `same-net-coincident` snapshot | changed | unchanged |

Not included, because the repro does not need them once the lower bound is right: the same-net skips in the force loops, `ViaPossibilitiesSolver2`, `computeViaCountVariants`, and the closed-face check, and the boundary-clamp change. `computeViaCountVariants` (base-class setup only, not reached by `MultiHeadPolyLineIntraNodeSolver3`) still asks for two vias between connected coincident branches; that can follow separately through the same `connMap` if wanted.

Verified locally: the repro test, the new crossing-count test, and the 44 test files that touch the polyline solver, the portfolio solver, or `getIntraNodeCrossings` (52 pass, 6 skipped, 0 fail). The full suite and benchmarks were not run locally.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VREF fanout | [Before VREF](`` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/db273508af2915dd43c58afd83ada0b86a4178f5/tests/repro/__snapshots__/ecp5-vref-fanout-focused.snap.svg) `` | [After VREF](``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/d78c0c3a03cb1334a8bb874a6f344b183c0ba953/tests/repro/__snapshots__/ecp5-vref-fanout-focused.snap.svg) ``` |
