title: Add a browser entry point for pcb-mode short detection
description: Adds a browser-compatible entry point for detecting shorts in PCB mode, allowing on-demand loading from a CDN without Node-only dependencies.
body:
## Why

pcb-viewer wants a "Right Click > Check for Shorts" action that loads this package on demand from jscdn. The main entry can't be imported in a browser: 5 of its 13 static imports fail there.

| Import | In Chrome |
| --- | --- |
| `@resvg/resvg-js` | jscdn returns 500 (native Node addon) |
| `node:zlib` | jscdn returns 404 |
| `tscircuit`, `circuit-to-svg` | fail on their `debug` dependency (jscdn returns 500) |
| `gerber-to-svg` | throws while initialising |

The pure-JS "pcb" mode needs none of those.

## What

- New `lib/browser.ts`, built to `dist/browser.js` and exported as `@tscircuit/check-shorts/browser`. It exports `findBitmapShorts` and `renderBitmapShortDebug` with "pcb" mode only; "gerber" mode throws a clear error.
- `bitmap-short-detector.ts` no longer imports the gerber rasterizer. It exports `createBitmapShortDetector(gerberSupport?)`, and the new `node-bitmap-short-detector.ts` passes the gerber functions in. The main entry's exports and behaviour are unchanged.

Once released, the browser build is importable at:

```
https://jscdn.tscircuit.com/@tscircuit/check-shorts/latest/dist/browser.js/+esm
```

## Testing

- `bun test`: 62 pass, including a new `tests/browser-entry.test.ts` that bundles the browser entry and asserts it only imports the five packages that load in a browser.
- Loaded the built `dist/browser.js` in headless Chrome, with bare imports rewritten to jscdn URLs the way `+esm` does. It found the 2 pad/pour shorts in `usb-c-pad-pour-contact.json`.

## Known limitation, not addressed here

"pcb" mode rasterizes fills by testing every pixel against every polygon vertex, so boards with detailed copper pours are very slow. On a 70 x 60 mm 4-layer board, one inner-layer pour with 353 cutouts did not finish in 9 minutes at the default resolution. In a browser that would freeze the tab, so a scanline fill (or the native canvas) is worth doing before relying on this for large boards.

title: Add native firmware for the NEMA14 RP2040 V2
description: Adds a dedicated RP2040 firmware target for the NEMA14 V2 PCB, including its TMP102 on IC0, two signed winding-current ADC channels, a distinct protocol ID, and a CI UF2 artifact.
body:
Adds a dedicated RP2040 firmware target for the [NEMA14 V2 PCB](https://tscircuit.com/AnasSarkiz/NEMA14_RP2040_V2), including its TMP102 on I²C0, two signed winding-current ADC channels, a distinct protocol ID, and a CI UF2 artifact. The V1 target keeps its original pinout.

Local Pico SDK 2.3.1 build, native regression suite, and NEMA14 dashboard test passed. Flashed the connected V2 with ROM readback verification. Its disabled-driver diagnostic counted 320 pulses. Forward and reverse 40-full-step moves each counted 640 pulses and completed with zero underruns. The driver returned to sleep.

With the initial wiring, the motor vibrated and winding-current snapshots reached about ±1.25 A. After the operator rearranged the leads, the same test produced confirmed shaft rotation in both directions and reported up to 0.30 A per winding. The driver finished disabled and asleep at 25.4 °C. Phase currents are uncalibrated. DATA voltage telemetry read approximately 2.48 V during active USB and still needs a meter check.

title: test: check IBIS pin inspection and edge duration on real vendor files
description: Adds tests for IBIS pin inspection and edge duration using real vendor files, ensuring proper verification of vendor models and their integration into the testing framework.
body:
Stacked on #141. Five TSX channel fixtures rendered through core check vendor pin selection, capabilities, rail ports and voltages, typical 10–90% edges, and default capture duration. The level shifter uses a 3.3 V B side and a 1.8 V A side.

CI fetches and verifies the six locked vendor models, caches them by the lock file hash, and runs all five vendor tests. `ci.yml` omits `bun run lint`. The inspection boards are not autorouted. Each has one hand-placed trace and no reference pour. The tests inspect pins and converter metadata without running a simulation. SN74V245 has ramp data only and cannot switch, so its test checks the ramp estimate and rails.

The lock-file trim includes the inherited `rs485` and `cmos` entries and the inherited top-level fields `formatVersion` and `vendorFilesRedistributed`. Nothing through #112 reads the removed fields.

### New concepts

`IBIS_MODEL_DIR` points to the verified vendor files. Locally, set it and run `bun run fetch:vendor-models` before running the tests. The five tests fail when the directory is unset and verify each model's SHA-256 before using it. See the [vendor model fetch instructions](https://github.com/tscircuit/signal-integrity-pipeline/blob/43884f28fdf128414184809cab9f4577880c3c09/docs/vendor-ibis-models.md).

Carries the `chore: clear inherited lint warnings` commit for warnings inherited from main.

body:
The September report previously used legacy sponsorship amounts and public expense visibility. title: Use fixed-endpoint via clearance in B01 detailed routing
description: Updates the B01 dependency to improve routing efficiency and validation for high-density designs, specifically addressing through-vias near fixed endpoints.
body:
Use the merged B01 fix for through-vias near fixed endpoints in high-density routing and regional repair. This updates the B01 dependency from `7ca0fef` to the `main` commit `a224564`. Its Git tree matches the revision tested on the DDR boards. [B01 commit](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/commit/a224564f52635bb5dc8d120d43ef71f9437c7393) · [Visual repro #27](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/27) · [Solver fix #28](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/28)

On the Allwinner A64 native assignment, B01 now completes all 12 paths in one window, up from 8. The 12 paths pass endpoint, route-to-route and fixed-copper clearance checks. On the first blocked STM32MP157 window, it rejects the physically impossible via in 147 iterations, down from 42,031. Across all 543 B01 windows on the two boards, one gains completion and none lose it.

Running all ten original DDR TSX designs through tscircuit 0.0.3275 (Core 0.0.2456 and capacity-autorouter 0.0.1149) gives 6 complete boards and 422 of 606 connected nets, with zero physical findings on the exported copper before and after. H616 and ButterStick together use five additional vias. The 225 fixed traces and 326 fixed vias remain byte-identical. The A64 board still stops in an earlier routing window. The STM32MP157 board still requires a new global assignment.

The B01 obstacle benchmark solves and physically validates 100 of 100 cases on both versions. Mean search iterations drop from 1,315 to 1,167.

The existing routing snapshots were regenerated on Linux. The MIDI keyboard retains both USB vias and their endpoints, the SRJ33 pair repair preserves its fixed copper and terminal anchors, and both pass DRC. The H616 reference fixture still routes 109 nets and passes trace continuity and board clearance. The separate H616 ZQ1 crossing passes its fixed-copper checks and preserves its focused snapshot. BeaglePlay routes all 51 traces to their 102 ports with zero DRC or port findings. The native H616 and ButterStick snapshots show the additional vias on the two complete DDR designs.

The B01 PRs include GitHub-diffable whole-board and detail snapshots for both designs, plus the exact A64 input and the minimized STM32MP157 input. [Board sources](https://github.com/ShiboSoftwareDev/core-ddr-benchmark/tree/24dc44c166d4258c3538f8b1f66953f1b6f58690) · [Paired visual diffs](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/28/files)

A fresh install of the published tscircuit package reproduced all ten baseline boards and all 94 recorded circuit, phase and finding artifacts byte for byte. All nine autorouter test groups passed with the identical B01 tree on the pre-merge pin. [Pre-merge CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/44966809965) · [Current PR checks](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/4077/checks)

title: Speed up repeated via checks in DDR detailed routing
description: Optimizes the detailed routing process by caching occupant lists for repeated via checks, resulting in significant runtime improvements across various boards.
body:
B01 repeatedly scans every layer around the same candidate via. Pin [B01 #25](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/25) to reuse that occupant list during each route search, clearing it before the next search so committed routes and rip-ups are observed. [Native STM32 repro](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/24).

| Whole board through Core, B01 main → cache | Before | After | Faster |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [STM32MP157](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/44958343949) | 203.4 s | 168.1 s | **17%** |
| [i.MX6](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/44958539685) | 159.2 s | 134.5 s | **15%** |

[All ten real TSX boards](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/44956381961) keep identical copper, native routing inputs, connectivity, via counts and zero physical findings on the exported copper. The update also includes B01 main's already-merged fixed-wire rasterization optimization. The full update also improves ButterStick by 6%; the other boards' timings vary between −3.3% and +1.9%. Both exact autorouter commits were built and run through tscircuit 0.0.3273 / Core 0.0.2452 on the same ARM runner per board.

title: Use B01’s bounded fixed-wire rasterization
description: Implements B01s bounded fixed-wire rasterization to optimize the routing process by reducing unnecessary cell checks for long wires, improving CPU time and maintaining routing accuracy.
body:
Use B01's bounded fixed-wire rasterization. For long wires, B01 was testing the exact intersection between the wire and thousands of grid cells far outside the copper. The new bounds check skips those cells and preserves the existing exact test for cells that touch the clearance boundary. [Two native visual repros](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/21) · [Solver fix and SVG diffs](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/22)

I replayed the full remaining-routing phase on H616 and iCEPi. At each B01 setup I compared every cell's trace and via owners with those produced by the published B01. All 607 grids matched.

| Board | B01 windows | Exact cell tests on release | With this pin | Reduction |

| H616 | 273 | 7,736,611 | 3,354,427 | 56.6% |
| iCEPi | 334 | 9,065,288 | 3,012,629 | 66.8% |

On 55 separately captured repair inputs, median setup CPU time for the set fell from 2.58 s to 0.97 s across seven paired passes. Three paired runs of the whole H616 remaining phase used median CPU time of 65.4 s and 63.4 s, respectively. A repeat on 0.0.3269 with the workers pinned to the same logical CPU gave 67.3 s and 65.1 s. All twelve runs produced identical routes. Local timings came from a shared machine.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end DDR board validation</summary>

I ran the original TSX on published tscircuit 0.0.3269, Core 0.0.2447 and autorouter 0.0.1145, then repeated every board with the router built from this PR. The native fanout, bus-lane phases, default router and electrical checks ran on both revisions. [Board definitions and TSX](https://github.com/ShiboSoftwareDev/core-ddr-benchmark/tree/24dc44c166d4258c3538f8b1f66953f1b6f58690/circuits)

| OrangeCrab | 50/50 | 50/50 |
| i.MX6 | 53/53 | 53/53 |

| ButterStick | 55/55 | 55/55 |

Both versions connect 422/606 nets. All emitted trace and via records match byte for byte, including 225 fixed traces and 326 associated via records. Six boards pass every electrical check. The other four retain the same connectivity failures. Physical checks found zero violations on the emitted copper across all ten.

On H3, A13 and A64, committing bus traces stranded 14 future terminals in a sampled pad-escape check. Removing a specific bus trace per terminal restored an escape. The pending bus-solver change restored all eight H3 escapes in a replay, after which global search exhausted its two-million-step budget. title: Keep through-vias clear of fixed endpoints on other nets
description: Fixes routing issues by ensuring through-vias do not collide with fixed endpoints on different nets, improving routing efficiency and accuracy.
body:
Stacked on [visual repro #27](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/pull/27).

A through-via crosses every routing layer. B01 previously treated copper beside a fixed endpoint as something it could rip up. The new grid records which net owns the endpoint clearance around each legal via center, using the physical center of the via and the original endpoint coordinates. Search skips a site if it would collide with another net’s endpoint. Branches of the same net can still share copper.

| Native case | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A64 assigned paths in the captured window | 8/12 | **12/12** |
| A64 local search iterations / rip-ups | 584,437 / 200 | **22,526 / 10** |
| STM32MP157 first failing window, iterations / rip-ups | 42,031 / 200 | **147 / 0** |
| STM32MP157 two-pair visual reduction, iterations / rip-ups | 125,548 / 200 | **145 / 0** |

All 12 A64 paths reach their assigned endpoints. Independent checks cover route-to-route clearance and all 302 fixed high-density route sections at the board’s 0.10668 mm margin. Across all 283 A64 and 260 STM32MP157 B01 inputs reconstructed from the native tscircuit 0.0.3275 run, completed windows rise from 396 to 397. Every formerly completed window still completes. Via-to-foreign-endpoint violations in intermediate output drop from 40 to zero. Two pre-existing local clearance findings remain in a different A64 window.

| Full TSX suite | tscircuit 0.0.3275 | With this change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fully connected DDR boards | 6/10 | 6/10 |
| Connected nets | 422/606 | 422/606 |
| Physical findings on exported copper | 0 | 0 |
| Exported vias | 843 | 848 |

H616 adds one via and 13.41 mm of trace. ButterStick adds four vias and 14.39 mm. All 225 fixed traces and 326 fixed vias match the release byte for byte. A64 still fails in an earlier routing window. STM32MP157 now reports that its assigned through-via has no legal site without exhausting the rip-up budget.

The tests check both the new clearance and legal sharing with a same-net branch. In the existing B02 cross-layer case the first pass routes 8 of 9 pairs, up from 7. Its alternate search uses 658 iterations, up from 508, and its repair uses 1,072, down from 2,105. The test retains bounds on both. The package passed 80 tests with two existing skips, type checking and formatting. Both versions solved and physically validated all 100 standard B01 obstacle benchmark cases. Mean iterations fell from 1,315 to 1,167.

| Allwinner A64 | STM32MP157 |
| --- | --- |
| ![A64 with all twelve assigned paths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/b1b2e437f166ceffca99eaa29dc48d427fd2df5a/tests/b01/__snapshots__/a64-fixed-port-routing-window.snap.svg) | ![STM32MP157 with the fixed endpoint protected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/b1b2e437f166ceffca99eaa29dc48d427fd2df5a/tests/b01/__snapshots__/stm32mp157-via-at-fixed-port.snap.svg) |

B01 checks the exact intersection between a fixed wire’s clearance and each candidate grid cell. On a long straight wire, the initial square covers thousands of cells far from the copper. Compute the wire’s padded bounds once and skip the exact test for cells outside them. Cells touching the boundary still receive the existing geometry test.

title: Reuse known clear and blocked segments in DDR bus visibility searches
description: Optimizes visibility checks in DDR bus routing by reusing known clear and blocked segments, significantly reducing the number of segment checks required during routing calculations.
body:
Third in the stack. #231 captures the two DDR boards, and #234 corrects the pad outlines in their debug view. While expanding one visibility-graph vertex, several candidate paths start along the same horizontal or vertical axis. A clear segment proves every shorter segment along that ray is clear. A blocked segment rules out any longer one. The checker keeps the clear coordinate interval and the nearest known block on either side of the vertex. Diagonal segments and later legs go through the existing geometry test. A custom board outline checks the requested segment before a cached clear result is used. | Captured Core phase | Segment checks before | Segment checks after | Reduction | Connectivity after solve | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | A13 second RAM byte | 54,500,477 | 20,147,729 | 63.0% | 32/32 | | A64 third byte | 49,056,210 | 22,104,261 | 54.9% | 24/24 | Both phases pass copper DRC and preserve their supplied traces. Both committed SVGs match #234 byte for byte apart from the check counts in their captions. [Completed A13 snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/675481ea2c5f8f7b7b575f5c65175effcb4af6ba/tests/__snapshots__/a13-ram-byte1-visibility.snap.svg) · [Completed A64 snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/675481ea2c5f8f7b7b575f5c65175effcb4af6ba/tests/__snapshots__/a64-byte2-visibility.snap.svg) `bun test tests/visibility-from-one-vertex.test.ts tests/a13-ram-byte1-visibility.test.ts tests/a64-byte2-visibility.test.ts` All ten native TSX designs also ran through tscircuit 0.0.3272 with this revision bundled into Core. Six boards completed and 422/606 requested nets connected on both revisions. All 496 trace and 843 via records and all 79 stage artifacts matched. In three alternating runs per revision on the same logical CPU, median CPU for the two targeted bus phases changed from 60.7 s to 37.9 s on A13 and from 38.8 s to 24.6 s on A64. ## AM3352 benchmark Both revisions passed 11/11 placements and connected 517/517 signals. Per-placement connectivity, copper DRC, length matching, pair coupling and fixed fanout validation matched. Aggregate solver time was 1,509.4 s before and 1,585.4 s after (+5.0%). The largest increases were control-inner1 (425.5 s to 470.5 s) and outer-layers (522.8 s to 547.9 s). Each placement had one paired fresh solve on Blacksmith Linux with four vCPUs, Bun 1.4.0 and a 3,600-second budget per revision. Base `d929813671f600a47f5b956051e05a3d899e0434`, head `675481ea2c5f8f7b7b575f5c65175effcb4af6ba`. The workflow runs `bun base/scripts/pr-benchmark/run-pair.ts` for all eleven declared samples, using the base harness and validating both solver entries. title: Draw rotated bus pads at their footprint dimensions
description: Draws rotated bus pads at their footprint dimensions, ensuring accurate clearance checks against the pads in the bus solvers debug view.
body:
Second in the stack, based on #231. The routing optimization in #232 builds on this visual. The A13 CPU has 1.475 × 0.20 mm pads at a 45° angle, on a 0.40 mm pitch. The bus solver checks clearance against the rotated pads. Its debug view drew the 1.18 mm square around each one, obscuring the 0.20 mm gap between neighboring pins. Pass the original obstacle dimensions, center, layer and `ccwRotationDegrees` to the rectangle in `graphics-debug`, following the native board snapshot scripts. The A13 snapshot now shows all 176 peripheral CPU pins at their footprint dimensions. The regression checks the pad on both of its copper layers. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![A13 CPU pads drawn as squares](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/08e709729e112563c24677cdde065422f560fe86/tests/__snapshots__/a13-ram-byte1-visibility.snap.svg) | ![A13 CPU pads drawn at their footprint rotation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/d929813671f600a47f5b956051e05a3d899e0434/tests/__snapshots__/a13-ram-byte1-visibility.snap.svg) | ## Verification Fresh native solves passed connectivity and copper DRC for 32/32 A13 connections and 24/24 A64 connections. A13 took 54,500,477 segment checks and A64 took 49,056,210 on both revisions. The A64 comparison already matches its checked-in snapshot. `bun test tests/iteration-zero-visualization.test.ts tests/a13-ram-byte1-visibility.test.ts tests/a64-byte2-visibility.test.ts` ## AM3352 benchmark Both revisions passed 11/11 placements and connected 517/517 signals. Per-placement connectivity, copper DRC, length matching, pair coupling and fixed fanout validation matched. Aggregate solver time was 1,645.0 s before and 1,618.7 s after (-1.6%). The largest increases were outer-layers (506.1 s to 530.4 s) and inner-layers-left (116.7 s to 121.6 s). Each placement had one paired fresh solve on Blacksmith Linux with four vCPUs, Bun 1.4.0 and a 3,600-second budget per revision. Base `08e709729e112563c24677cdde065422f560fe86`, head `d929813671f600a47f5b956051e05a3d899e0434`. The workflow runs `bun base/scripts/pr-benchmark/run-pair.ts` for all eleven declared samples, using the base harness and validating both solver entries. title: Reproduce repeated visibility checks on the A13 and A64 DDR buses
description: Adds tests to reproduce visibility checks for the A13 and A64 DDR buses, ensuring connectivity and copper clearance are maintained during routing.
body:
First in the stack. #234 renders the pad outlines at their footprint rotation, and #232 reduces the visibility checks for the same routes. Run two completed DDR bus phases from the ten-board TSX benchmark through the default bus pipeline. Each fixture is the adapter input captured from tscircuit 0.0.3271, Core 0.0.2450 and bus-lanes-solver 0.0.63. Earlier copper retains its original trace IDs and via spans. The fixtures contain 378 and 607 pad obstacles respectively. | Native Core phase | Earlier routes | New routes | Connected after solve | Segment visibility checks | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | A13 second RAM byte | 24 | 8 | 32/32 | 54,500,477 | | A64 third byte | 16 | 8 | 24/24 | 49,056,210 | A CPU profile of both native phases put the repeated checks in the vector visibility search. Each SVG shows the completed routing and the observed check count. The tests also verify copper clearance, original endpoints, and preservation of the supplied routes. Previous connection definitions are used only in the validator so that routing sees the same input as Core. Run `bun test tests/a13-ram-byte1-visibility.test.ts tests/a64-byte2-visibility.test.ts`. Both passed on the pinned release solver. The change adds benchmark fixtures and tests. The required fresh eleven-sample comparison runs in the AM3352 benchmark workflow. [Source TSX circuits](https://github.com/ShiboSoftwareDev/core-ddr-benchmark/tree/24dc44c166d4258c3538f8b1f66953f1b6f58690/circuits) ## Verification from the final revision ### tscircuit 0.0.3272 confirmation Core 0.0.2451 and fanout-solver 0.0.100 still produce both exact adapter inputs and the preceding net definitions in these fixtures. Fresh solves reproduced the same visibility counts. I reran all ten TSX boards on the new release and the integrated fix. Both connected 422/606 nets, six boards completed and every one of the 496 trace and 843 via records matched. All 79 captured routing inputs, outputs and checkpoints also matched. title: feat: check that routed copper connects each driver to its receivers
description: Check that selected routed copper connects each driver to its receivers and follows a linear path. The check raises channel_fanout for a branch, channel_net for disconnected copper, and channel_driver_terminal_missing or channel_receiver_terminal_missing for missing PCB terminals in strict mode.
body:
Check that selected routed copper connects each driver to its receivers and follows a linear path. The check raises `channel_fanout` for a branch, `channel_net` for disconnected copper, and `channel_driver_terminal_missing` or `channel_receiver_terminal_missing` for missing PCB terminals in strict mode.

Stacked on #141. The geometry dependency PR adds direct pins for `@flatten-js/core` and `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` below #117. The first callers of `signalTopology` and `validateSignalGraph` are in #99.

### New concepts

- **Copper point.** Each route endpoint is snapped to a 0.00001 mm grid and keyed by layer so coincident points have a stable identity.
- **Junction.** Touching pad and via outlines on the same layer share a node. A via connects the layers it spans, and overlapping contacts along a wire share a junction.
- **Routed copper graph.** Edges connect consecutive junctions along traces and the terminals of series passives. The graph follows copper selected for the signal and excludes unrelated nets and rails.
- **Branch rule.** A routed driver may have at most one physical neighbor. Each other junction on its reachable path may have at most two.
- **Cross-leg load.** A passive between the positive and negative legs loads both legs while leaving their graph paths separate.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Select signal nets and copper] --> B[Find contacts and order junctions]
  B --> C[Connect series passives]
  C --> D[Check branches and receiver reachability]
```

Same-layer trace, pad and via outlines connect when they overlap or are separated by up to 0.00001 mm. This includes trace ends that miss each other's centerlines, via-in-pad without a launch trace on the pad layer, and overlapping via rings.

title: feat: declare aggressor controls for channel simulations
description: Add optional aggressor_pattern and aggressor_disabled fields to PCB transient channel simulation records, allowing for more precise control over aggressor behavior in simulations.
body:
Add optional `aggressor_pattern` and `aggressor_disabled` fields to PCB transient channel simulation records. Aggressors are output-capable pins coupled to the simulation’s channels, excluding the driver pins of all channels in that simulation. The channels keep their own `pattern` and `driver_disabled` settings.

The schema trims the optional pattern, rejects blank patterns, and preserves omitted fields and explicit booleans. The reference documents that `true` requests high impedance for every aggressor and takes precedence over the pattern. See [props #1058](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/1058) and [core #5804](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5804) for the TSX props and serialization.

title: Declare schematic length units on geometry records and subcircuits
description: Adds optional schematic_length_unit to 18 schematic record types for specifying geometry length units, supporting mm, in, and a legacy unit.
body:
This adds optional `schematic_length_unit` to the 18 schematic record types that carry drawing geometry and to `source_failed_to_create_component_error`, which can carry a `schematic_center`. The field accepts `"mm"`, `"in"`, or the legacy unit `"9.236363636363636mm"`. The TypeScript type is explicit.

`source_group.default_schematic_length_unit` declares a subcircuit's default for writing new geometry. Each record describes its own stored numbers. A missing record tag means legacy units, even when a subcircuit declares another default. Sheet paper dimensions always use millimeters.

The schema preserves numeric geometry and optional tags on parse. Tests cover a standalone trace, legacy records, a mixed-unit document, and a diagnostic with schematic and PCB coordinates. Unit conversion belongs in producers and consumers.

title: Rotate hole shapes and offsets in transformPCBElement
description: Fixes the rotation of hole shapes and offsets in PCB elements to ensure proper alignment and clearance during autorouting, addressing issues with overlapping holes and pads.
body:
`transformPCBElement` and `transformPCBElements` moved `pcb_plated_hole` and `pcb_hole` x/y but left their rotation fields alone. A rotated component kept its slotted holes and rect hole pads in the original orientation. In core, this overlapped USB-C shell holes with GND pads after pack layout, and the resulting clearance error skipped autorouting for the whole board. This is the util half of https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/4021.

## Before and after

Stacked on #311, which records the two pictures below on `main`. This PR's diff then changes only those two snapshot files. INPUT is the hole as authored, EXPECTED is the 90 degree turn written out by hand, and ACTUAL is what `transformPCBElements` returns.

**Before** (`main`, from #311): only the plain pill plated hole turns.

![hole shapes before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/1e5e1b5be6ba1784e21630de6887138b00c9b45b/tests/__snapshots__/repro-hole-rotation-shapes.snap.svg)

**After** (this PR): every row matches EXPECTED.

![hole shapes after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/cfafafcc61727f298112d0883e22dfd4990bb56e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-hole-rotation-shapes.snap.svg)

**Before**, on the pads of KiCad's `BarrelJack_Horizontal`: the pads and silkscreen turn, the three slots do not.

![barrel jack before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/1e5e1b5be6ba1784e21630de6887138b00c9b45b/tests/__snapshots__/repro-hole-rotation-barrel-jack.snap.svg)

**After**:

![barrel jack after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/cfafafcc61727f298112d0883e22dfd4990bb56e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-hole-rotation-barrel-jack.snap.svg)

Polygon pads are not in the pictures, because the pinned `circuit-to-svg` (0.0.413) does not draw their `ccw_rotation`. They are covered by assertions.

## Core

Core needs nothing removed when it bumps to this. The temporary hole-rotation helper in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5160 never landed, because the stale bot closed that PR, and core's `applyPackOutput` calls plain `transformPCBElements`.

## Changes

Rotation fields now match what core's `PlatedHole` and `Hole` emit for an explicit `pcbRotation`:

| Element | Field |
| --- | --- |
| `pcb_plated_hole` `pill`, `oval`, `hole_with_polygon_pad` | `ccw_rotation` |
| `pcb_plated_hole` `circular_hole_with_rect_pad` | `rect_ccw_rotation` |
| `pcb_plated_hole` `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad` | `hole_ccw_rotation`, `rect_ccw_rotation` |
| `pcb_plated_hole` `pill_hole_with_rect_pad` | becomes `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad` |
| `pcb_hole` `pill` | becomes `rotated_pill` |
| `pcb_hole` `rotated_pill` | `ccw_rotation` |

Solder paste is left to #304.

- Angles are normalized to `[0, 360)`, and float noise is snapped away, so -90.00000000000001 becomes 270.
- Pure translations change nothing, including the shape of an unrotated pill.
- Mirrored matrices use `getTransformedRectRotation` and reduce to `[0, 180)`, since these shapes repeat every 180 degrees. A Y flip keeps an axis-aligned `pill` as `pill`.
- Polygon pad outlines flip under a mirror, because they can be asymmetric.
- `hole_offset_x/y` now turn with the hole. They are board-world vectors, so otherwise a rotated pad leaves its drill behind. This differs from core's `PlatedHole`, which emits them unrotated and has that bug for an explicit `pcbRotation`.

## Downstream

- **tscircuit/easyeda-converter:** `getEasyEdaPlatedHoleGeometry` emits rotations already in the final Y-up frame, then applies `scale(1, -1)` through this transform. It's pinned at `^0.0.128`, so nothing changes until it bumps. At that bump, non-quarter-turn holes get mirrored twice unless it emits the pre-flip angle or excludes holes from the transform.

## Overlapping PRs

#304, now merged, rotates `pill` and `oval` plated holes and moves rect and pill paste through its own transform. The merge of `main` into this branch drops #304's plated hole clause, since this PR's code covers those shapes too and keeping both rotated them twice. #304's USB1046 test passes unchanged.

#277, #191 and #131, still open, rotate these same fields. Rotation isn't idempotent, so only one of them can land with this one, and the others need closing or rebasing.

- #277 and #131 swap plated hole dimensions and also rotate the fields, so a hole that already has a rotation field turns twice on a quarter turn. Core keeps the dimensions and uses the field.
- #191 is the closest to this PR, including the hole offsets. It conflicts with `main`. It also covers the missing polygon `ccw_rotation` case below, which this PR doesn't.

#130 isn't linked as closing. Its expected output is swapped `rect_pad_width` and `rect_pad_height`, and here the turn goes in `rect_ccw_rotation` instead.

## Not changed

- `pcb_hole` `oval` and `rect`, and `pcb_solder_paste` `oval`, have no rotation field, so they don't turn. Core's `Hole` does the same.
- A polygon pad with no `ccw_rotation` is treated as 0. `getPlatedHolePolygon` falls back to the component's rotation when the field is missing, so on a component that was already rotated, the pad ends up short by that rotation. Current core emits the field, so this only affects older or hand-written circuit JSON.

## Testing

- `bun test` (209 pass), `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `biome format` are clean.
- Both snapshot tests from #311 fail on this branch until their pictures are regenerated, which is the last commit here.
- The `"files"` reformat in `package.json` now comes from #311. Each release bump commit expands that line, so Format Check fails on `main` after every release.

- Per-shape expectations are ported from the core helper's unit test.
- Property tests check that pill axes, polygon vertices and drill centers end up where the matrix sends them, across rotations and mirrors.
- A parity test compares against what core emits for an explicit `pcbRotation`. It covers the 4 shapes the pinned `tscircuit` devDependency rotates. All 6 shapes were also checked once by hand against current core source, on the top layer.

Rechecked on 2026-11-21, after the merge of `main`:

- An independent geometry check pushes each shape's pad corners, hole axis ends and drill center through 7 matrices (translation, 90, -90 with packer float noise, 180, 45, Y flip, Y flip plus 90) and compares them with the transformed element. It covers the plated-hole shapes other than polygon pads, plus `pcb_hole` pills. On `main` (0.0.132) 33 of 70 cases are wrong: `pill` and `oval` plated holes are right, and the rect-pad shapes and `pcb_hole` pills are not. On this branch all 70 match.
- Core's packed USB-C repro (C165948 shell pills, connector turned to 270 by the packer) gives 0 clearance errors and 4 traces with this build, the same as with 0.0.132, so #304's fix is not applied twice.
- 24 core test files (rect-pad holes, polygon pads, packing, circuit JSON inflation, USB-C; 27 tests) give the same result on this build as on util 0.0.131 and 0.0.132: 23 pass, and the same 4 fail locally on all three.

Core's full snapshot suite has not been run against this change.

title: Return null from cju lookups that find nothing
description: Changes cju lookups to return null instead of undefined when no matches are found, preventing TypeErrors in circuit routing.
body:
`cju(...)` lookups returned `undefined` when nothing matched. `get`, `getWhere`, `getUsing` and `select` are typed `| null`, and `cjuIndexed` returns `null`.

## Why it matters

A caller that follows the types and filters with `!== null` keeps the missing entry. Core does this in `getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson`, which builds its db with `su(...)`:

```ts
const connectedPcbPorts = trace.connected_source_port_ids
  .map((sourcePortId) => db.pcb_port.getWhere({ source_port_id: sourcePortId }))
  .filter((pcbPort): pcbPort is PcbPort => pcbPort !== null)
// ...
if (connectedPort.x === undefined || ...   // TypeError when connectedPort is undefined
```

One traced port with no pads is enough, for example a `<connector standard="usb_c">` whose footprint fetch failed. Autorouting throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'connectedPort.x')` and the whole board is left with 0 traces.

## Change

- `cju`: `get`, `getWhere`, `getUsing` and `select` return `null` when nothing matches.
- `select` also returns `null` for element types it doesn't handle. It used to fall through and return `undefined`.
- `cjuIndexed` is unchanged. It already returned `null`.

## Behavior change

title: Bump circuit-json-util to 0.0.133 so packed slots rotate
description: Fixes autorouting failure due to unrotated plated holes in packed USB-C connectors, allowing successful routing of the board.
body:
A bare `<connector standard="usb_c">` with no position leaves the whole board unrouted, with "Autorouting was skipped because 2 PCB placement errors were found". This still happens with tscircuit 0.0.3280.

## Cause

The pack layout turns J1 a quarter turn and moves its elements with `transformPCBElements`. Up to circuit-json-util 0.0.131, that function doesn't update the rotation of `pill`/`oval` plated holes. The SHELL slots stay upright and overlap GND1/GND2 (-0.159mm for C165948, -0.1mm for the default part). That raises `pcb_pad_pad_clearance_error`, and autorouting is skipped. An explicit `pcbRotation` was never affected.

circuit-json-util 0.0.133 ([#304](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/pull/304)) rotates those holes. Forcing it into tscircuit 0.0.3280 makes both parts route cleanly.

## Changes

- `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` `^0.0.131` → `^0.0.133`. 0.0.134 and later need circuit-json 0.0.560, which #5791 is adopting, so those releases (including [#293](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/pull/293)'s rect-pad hole shapes) are left to that PR.
- `tests/repros/repro-usbc-packed-rotation-shell-pad-overlap.test.tsx`: usb_c C165948 (existing fixture) and a `dip20` on a 30x30mm board. The packer turns J1 to 270°. It fails on 0.0.131 (slot rotation 0) and passes on 0.0.133, with no pad-pad errors and traces routed.

## Snapshot changes

0.0.133 also rotates `pcb_fabrication_note_text`, as it already did for silkscreen text. All 12 updated snapshots come from that:

- `pack-with-explicit-positioning`, `repro126-courtyard-rotation`: a packed LED rotated 90° kept its "+"/"-" fab text at 0°. It now gets 90°, which matches what `pcbRotation={90}` gives on main.
- `repro116-arduino-uno-*` (KiCad import into `<subcircuit circuitJson>`): 59 fab texts used to pick up the footprint rotation (90°/180°) even though the KiCad import has them at 0. They now keep the source rotation. The text extents move the drawing bounds, which shifts the whole image by about 2px, so the PNG diff is about 10%. Two of the stacked reroute comparisons route a little differently, and their assertions still pass.
- `repro60`: one trace detour moves by under 0.1mm.
- `repro58`: the packed D1 is turned 180°, so its "+"/"-" fab text now turns 180° too. Those glyphs look the same either way, and the rendered difference on CI is one pixel.
- The center-reroute snapshots for `repro116` also drop 16 LED fab paths per board. Current main no longer produces those paths (it outputs 240, the same as this branch). The old snapshot only passed because of that test's 0.15% threshold.

The second commit regenerates `repro58`, `repro116-arduino-uno` (after inflation) and both `repro116-arduino-uno-reroute-center` snapshots in a linux/amd64 bun 1.4.2 container. The first CI run failed on them, and they don't reproduce on macOS.

## Testing

I ran the full suite locally on this branch and on main (`ce2683b`) and compared failures. Tests that failed only on the branch were rerun one file at a time on both. The snapshots above were the only real differences; the rest also failed on main, or passed when run alone. Typecheck and format are clean.

Replaces #5160, which patched the transform inside core and was closed as stale.

title: Make default pin header and two-pin connector schematic boxes pass schematic-placement
description: Fixes default schematic box sizing for pin headers and two-pin connectors to comply with schematic placement checks.
body:
Two default schematic boxes fail `tsci check schematic-placement` before the author has written a single `sch*` prop. This makes both pass by default.

## What was wrong

**Labelled pin header.** A single-column `<pinheader>` with `pinLabels` got the generic box width (longest label × 0.1 + 1.1), so a five-pin header labelled `RUN DIR STEP nFAULT GND` came out 1.7 wide. The checker reports `PinHeaderSchematicBoxTooWide` and suggests 0.77.

**Two-pin connector.** A `<connector>` with two pins and no arrangement put one pin on each side of the box. On power and ground nets the checker reports `TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` and suggests rotating it, but schematic boxes do not rotate, so the hint cannot be followed.

```tsx
<pinheader
  name="J1"
  pinCount={5}
  pinLabels={["RUN", "DIR", "STEP", "nFAULT", "GND"]}
/>
<connector
  name="J2"
  footprint="jst2_p2.5mm_xh"
  pinLabels={{ pin1: "VM", pin2: "GND" }}
  connections={{ pin1: "net.VM", pin2: "net.GND" }}
/>
```

## What changes

- **Pin header:** when the pins are in one column and `schWidth` is not set, the box is sized to its labels: the longest label plus padding on both edges, and never narrower than the widest label's glyphs need. This is the same width the checker suggests, so the example above goes from 1.7 to 0.77.
- **Two-pin connector:** with no `schPinArrangement` / `schPortArrangement`, both pins are drawn on the right side with pin 1 on top, matching pin headers and connectors that already get a single column from their `standard`.

An explicit `schWidth` or pin arrangement is left exactly as it was.

`NormalComponent` gains two overridable hooks, `_getDefaultSchematicBoxWidth` and `_getDefaultSchematicBoxPortArrangement`, both returning `undefined` by default, so no other component changes.

## Tests

- `pin-header-default-schematic-box-width.test.tsx`: default widths for plain, wide-glyph and `N_`-prefixed labels, an explicit `schWidth` left alone, and `checkSchematicPlacement` reporting no box warnings.
- `connector-two-pin-default-schematic-arrangement.test.tsx`: both ports on the right with pin 1 above pin 2, and an explicit top/bottom arrangement left alone. `@tscircuit/checks` does not run the two-pin rule yet, so this asserts the port sides directly.
- Both tests fail on `main` and pass here.
- Built with this branch and no `sch*` props, the two examples above print no issues from the released CLI's `tsci check schematic-placement`.

## Snapshot changes

17 existing schematic snapshots change. Every one is in a test that contains a pin header or a two-pin connector: the header box shrinks to its labels, or the connector's pins move to one side. Nothing else in those schematics moves.

## Not included

A chip or connector with four or more labelled pins in a single column is still flagged as slightly too wide, because core estimates 0.1 per label character and the checker 0.095. Closing that gap would shift most chip snapshots, so it is left for a separate change.

title: Write rotated_rect solder paste as rotated regions instead of %LR
description: Changes the representation of rotated solder paste from using LR to using rotated regions, ensuring accurate rendering in Gerber files.
body:
Stacked on #272. Fixes #263

#134 stopped using `%LR` for rotated copper and solder mask, but `rotated_rect` paste still flashed the unrotated rectangle behind `%LR<angle>*%`, so readers that skip `%LR` draw the paste opening upright. Paste now uses the same rotated region as copper.

F_Paste for a 0.6 x 1.7 mm pad at 45 degrees:

Before
```
%LR45*%
X-01785000Y000901000D03*
%LR0*%
```
After
```
G36*
X-02598173Y001289909D02*
X-02173909Y001714173D01*
X-00971827Y000512091D01*
X-01396091Y000087827D01*
X-02598173Y001289909D01*
G37*
```

The repro test from #272 now checks that F_Paste has no `%LR` and that its outline matches F_Cu. F_Cu is gold, F_Paste is gray:

title: Add tsci inspect footprint <pathOrString>
description: Adds tsci inspect footprint pathOrString, which prints a footprints pins, pad positions, pad sizes, drill sizes and overall extents before the part is placed.
body:
Adds `tsci inspect footprint <pathOrString>`, which prints a footprint's pins, pad positions, pad sizes, drill sizes and overall extents before the part is placed.

Today the only way to see where pin 1 of a footprint string sits is a `node -e` one-liner against `@tscircuit/footprinter`, or building a board and reading the Circuit JSON.

```text
$ tsci inspect footprint jst2_p2.5mm_xh
jst2_p2.5mm_xh
source: footprinter string (@tscircuit/footprinter installed in this project)
parameters: fn=jst p=2.5 xh=true id=1 pw=1.7 pl=2 w=7.62 h=5.97 num_pins=2
pads: 2 plated holes
copper: 4.2 x 2 mm (x -2.1 to 2.1, y -1 to 1)
courtyard: 8.4 x 6.75 mm (x -4.2 to 4.2, y -3.9 to 2.85)

pin  kind         shape                        x      y  width  height  hole  layers
1    plated_hole  circular_hole_with_rect_pad  -1.25  0  1.7    2       1     top,bottom
2    plated_hole  pill                         1.25   0  1.7    2       1     top,bottom

Millimetres in the footprint's own frame (+x right, +y up), before pcbRotation.
```

## What the argument can be

| Input | Example | How it is loaded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Footprinter string | `soic8`, `pinrow4` | `fp.string(...)`; also prints the parsed parameters |
| Library footprint | `kicad:Resistor_SMD/R_0402_1005Metric`, `jlcpcb:C14877` | the platform config's `footprintLibraryMap`, the same loaders the build uses |
| File | `.kicad_mod`, a component `.tsx`, `.circuit.json` | the loader `tsci convert --footprinter` already uses |

For a component file the pin labels are shown next to the pin numbers (`1,VCC`). `--json` prints the same data as JSON.

A string footprinter cannot parse, an unknown library prefix, and a missing file each exit 1 with a message that says which one it was.

## Which footprinter is used

Footprinter strings are resolved with the project's own `@tscircuit/footprinter` when one is installed, so the pads match what `tsci build` will place, and fall back to the copy bundled with the CLI. The `source:` line says which was used. The two can differ: an older footprinter puts the JST pads above at y = 2.

## Structure

- `cli/inspect/register.ts` adds the `inspect` parent command.
- `cli/inspect/footprint/` holds the subcommand: loading, building the inspection, and formatting it.

## Tests

`tests/cli/inspect/inspect-footprint.test.ts` covers a footprinter string, `--json` with through-hole pads, a `.kicad_mod` file, a component file with pin labels, an unparseable string and a missing file. The `kicad:` and `jlcpcb:` lookups need the network and were checked by hand, not in tests.

The README help block is not regenerated here.

title: fix: never accept a refine candidate that creates a new copper contact
description: Fixes the autorouters behavior to reject candidates that introduce new copper contacts, preventing potential design rule violations during the routing process.
body:
Stacked on #3970. Pins high-density-repair03 main (c0325f3), which includes tscircuit/high-density-repair03#219.

The DRC engine names the other object on trace errors with typed ids (pcb_trace_ids, pcb_smtpad_id, pcb_plated_hole_id). A pcb_trace_error with actual_clearance < 0 is a short. Every final cleanup phase rejects a result with a short the current routes do not have: refine and safe-layer repair through isPipeline9DrcCandidateBetter({ candidateErrors, currentErrors, rejectNewContacts: true }), and via-pad projection through the same check. A short whose ids are missing or invalid counts as new. Shorts are keyed per pair of objects: the DRC engine merges every touching point between two objects into one error, so a second point is the same short.

The regional search before cleanup can still pass through a short that a later step removes. srj33 sample 3 needs that: its result removes seven input shorts and adds one, and forbidding it ends with 11 DRC issues instead of 3.

title: Complete STM32MP157 DDR routing through narrow BGA pad channels
description: Completes the routing of all 72 DDR nets for the STM32MP157 by implementing a new BGA escape routing solver that effectively utilizes narrow pad channels, ensuring all connections are electrically complete and meet clearance requirements.
body:
The released router connects the four STM32MP157 data bytes, then discards all 40 remaining nets. The global planner assigns all 97 branches, but detailed routing cannot fit the required through-vias inside its assigned cells.

| Before · 32/72 DDR nets connected | After · 72/72 DDR nets connected |
| --- | --- |
| [![Before STM32MP157 routing with 32/72 nets connected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/a28d4cd2b6d33ba29958e9544788b05c5474447d/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-stmp157-native-ddr-via-space.snap.svg)](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/a28d4cd2b6d33ba29958e9544788b05c5474447d/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-stmp157-native-ddr-via-space.snap.svg) | [![After STM32MP157 routing with 72/72 nets connected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/287ab0170d3c892203be434760862432ffac2f3a/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-stmp157-native-ddr-via-space.snap.svg)](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/287ab0170d3c892203be434760862432ffac2f3a/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-stmp157-native-ddr-via-space.snap.svg) |

Pipeline9 calls the standalone BGA solver after regional routing fails. This PR keeps board eligibility, signal-layer selection, endpoint validation, DRC and export in the autorouter. The solver package owns the grid, escape reservations and track search. The dependency is pinned to the merged `main` commit. [Solver PR and step debugger](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/pull/1) · [Pinned solver source](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/tree/f70041d56fef2f9136dff060ef654094f7fc67e0)

Between 0.4 mm BGA balls on a 0.8 mm pitch, a 0.127 mm trace with 0.127 mm clearance on each side has 0.019 mm of centerline freedom. The new solver aligns its grid to the balls, reserves the scarcest terminal exits first, and joins the original point pairs across cells. A reserved through-via reaches every signal layer with a single drill. New planar wires stay on layers used by surface terminals or real fixed wire segments. Pipeline9 accepts a full set of routes only after it passes the board’s clearance checks.

| STM32MP157 on tscircuit 0.0.3278 | Released | With this change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Electrically connected DDR nets | 32/72 | 72/72 |
| Disconnected PCB ports | 137 | 0 |
| Distinct drill sites | 56 | 246 |
| Physical clearance findings at 10⁻⁹ mm tolerance | 0 | 0 |

All 32 existing bus traces and 56 vias are byte-identical. Every new branch keeps its 0.127 mm width. All 190 added vias have a 0.327 mm land and a 0.2 mm drill. New wiring uses only top, inner2, inner4, inner5 and bottom, the five signal layers in the original KiCad stack. The TSX provides no length-skew or impedance targets. Replaying the existing detailed router with the same 137 legal pad escapes still failed on a later cell.

Running all ten original DDR TSX boards through the published tscircuit 0.0.3278 entry point raises electrical completion from 6/10 to 7/10 boards and from 422/606 to 462/606 nets. The other nine export byte-identical copper. The tighter checker reports the same five pre-existing findings on OrangeCrab, Glider and i.MX6. H3, A13 and A64 remain electrically incomplete.

The extraction was replayed against the in-repo fix at `225f73e8c` on the same ten TSX boards. All ten complete Circuit JSON exports match byte-for-byte. All captured routing-phase inputs and outputs match, as do both sets of physical clearance results. The STM32MP157 still connects 72/72 and has zero strict clearance findings. [Autorouter CI · 9/9 shards passed](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/45062224146)

The stacked PR updates the SVG from the native 710-pad, 32-fixed-trace repro. [Visual repro #4109](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/4109) · [Before and after in Files changed](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/4110/files#diff-7d9c76982c49a50f50d305868bd42a291ce3c7da3e05d6fba677c3b4ffff7c1a) · [Native board source](https://github.com/ShiboSoftwareDev/core-ddr-benchmark/tree/24dc44c166d4258c3538f8b1f66953f1b6f58690/circuits)

```sh
bun test --timeout 9999999 tests/features/bgaescaperoutingsolver tests/repro/pipeline9-stmp157-native-ddr-via-space.test.ts
```

title: Reproduce the RP2040 JST solder-pad offset in glTF
description: Reproduces the RP2040 JST solder-pad offset in glTF to ensure accurate placement of solder pads in the exported model.
body:
## Reproduction

[RP2040 motor controller v1.0.58](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller) places J1’s C265102 OBJ using `pcbRotation={270}`, `rotationOffset: 180`, and `positionOffset: { x: 2.9875, y: 0, z: -0.05 }`. The offset seats the model’s authored solder plane on the PCB. The native 3D viewer respects that origin, but the glTF exporter recenters the underside of the mesh and shifts J1 outward by 2.5 mm.

The offline fixture uses six synthetic OBJ contact faces and the released footprint, mounting transform, and copper rectangles. It exports and parses a GLB and checks that every contact face is inside its pad at the board surface. An explicit-origin control passes on current `main`.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repro/rp2040-jst-obj-origin.test.ts`
- Running the expected-failure case as a normal test on `main` reports `[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]` pad-contained triangles instead of `[2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2]`.
- The follow-up in #306 enables the regression as a normal test.

## Reproduction snapshot

The full C265102 JST housing and solder leads are visible. All four signal leads stop short of the gold pads. The snapshot uses the same OBJ as the published board.

![Full C265102 JST housing with misaligned solder leads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/66dd0795b3aeb1a5702991c8a794d60fe4f33164/tests/repro/__snapshots__/rp2040-jst-obj-origin.snap.png)

title: Preserve authored PCB OBJ anchors in glTF exports
description: Preserves the OBJs local origin when its CAD anchor is offset in the board plane from a known PCB footprint origin, ensuring accurate placement of solder contacts in glTF exports.
body:
Stacked on #305.

## Change

Preserve the OBJ’s local origin when its CAD anchor is offset in the board plane from a known PCB footprint origin and both generated alignment tags specify the board surface. The user's CAD position maps that local origin onto the board in the native viewer. Applying an additional inferred mesh offset in the exporter displaces the solder contacts.

An explicit `model_origin_position` takes precedence. The existing contact-centering path still handles unoffset CAD, alternate alignment settings, and non-OBJ formats, including the KiCad STEP case from #167.

## Validation

- The stacked regression goes from zero to all six contacts fully on their pads in the exported GLB.
- A separate export of the published v1.0.58 Circuit JSON and its actual C265102 OBJ confirmed all four signal leads and both anchor feet land within their pad outlines at the PCB surface.
- The explicit-origin, contact-centering, and TO-92 STEP controls pass.

## Corrected snapshot

The full C265102 JST model is shown from the same angle as #305. The four signal leads now extend onto the gold pads. The geometry test also verifies both mounting tabs.

title: Suppress coplanar outline seams across glTF mesh primitives
description: Suppresses visible seams in glTF mesh rendering by grouping outline edges of triangles from the same mesh instance, ensuring a continuous visual representation across material boundaries.
body:
PoppyGL previously extracted outline edges independently for each glTF primitive. Splitting a flat surface at a material boundary turned the shared diagonal into a visible line.

The glTF loader now tags primitives from the same mesh instance. Outline edge extraction groups triangles with that identity and the same placement, and section rendering uses their combined topology when closing cut loops. The shaded material pass still uses the original draw calls. Custom draw-call producers can supply the same identity explicitly.

The new visual regression shows a frame with an opening and a bent flange. The left panel uses separate nodes, and the right panel uses material primitives of one mesh. The single-mesh result matches an unsplit reference pixel for pixel, including with hidden edges enabled. The test also covers indexed draw calls, independently moved primitives, and a section through a split cube.

Verified all 94 Bun tests, type checking, formatting, and the package build. An integration check against circuit-json-to-drawing main produced byte-identical SVGs for the split and unsplit mesh using this PoppyGL build.

Related converter work: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/pull/20

title: Document schematic box sizing, sheet capacity, search sources and prop gaps
description: Adds documentation for schematic box sizing, sheet capacity, search sources, and prop gaps, improving user guidance for schematic design and component placement.
body:
## Why

In a recorded agent run that designed a NEMA17 stepper driver board, the PCB needed no rework, but the agent went through five schematic fix rounds and read `@tscircuit/core`, `@tscircuit/props` and `circuit-to-svg` source about ten times to answer questions the skill did not cover. It also tried to open `elements/schematicsheet.md`, which does not exist. This PR adds what it was looking for.

Every statement and example below was checked in a container against `tscircuit@0.0.3270` and `@tscircuit/cli@0.1.2482`.

## What changed

**New: `SCHEMATIC_PLACEMENT.md`**
- What `tsci check schematic-placement` prints, and that it exits 0 even when it lists issues.
- The defaults it flags before any layout work: a `<pinheader>` with `pinLabels` (`PinHeaderSchematicBoxTooWide`), a two-pin part on a power rail (`TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical`), and a chip with pins on all four sides (`SchematicBoxInnerLabelCollision`).
- Copy `suggestedSchWidth` / `suggestedSchHeight` / `deltaSchRotation` instead of estimating. The agent widened a box from 1.7 to 3.6 and got `GenericSchematicBoxTooWide` with a suggestion of 2.49.
- For a two-pin `<connector>`, `schPinArrangement` with top and bottom sides clears the issue; `schRotation` and `schOrientation` do not.
- After a schematic-only edit, rerun only this check.

**New: `elements/schematicsheet.md`**
- Props, including `sheetSize` (`"A4" | "ANSI_B"`).
- Capacity in schematic units: A4 is about 32.2 × 22.7, with about 31 × 21.6 usable.
- The sheet is centred on its contents.
- The build messages for overflow and for a non-default size.

**`CLI.md`, `SKILL.md`, `WORKFLOW.md`**
- Corrects "JLCPCB is searched when no source flag is supplied". A flagless `tsci search` queries all seven sources and waits for the slowest; in the run one search ended with `Failed to search mouser: The operation timed out.`
- Adds `--ti`, `--datasheets` and `TSCIRCUIT_DEFAULT_SEARCH_SOURCES`.
- Lists which checks accept a prebuilt `circuit.json` (`netlist` does not).

**Element pages**
- `via`: `tented`; a via on an SMD pad is a placement error, with a passing example that puts the via beside the pad and joins it with a pour.
- `net`, `board`: `nominalTraceWidth`, `defaultTraceWidth`, `minTraceWidth`, `defaultViaTenting`.
- `chip`: `noConnect`, `schWidth` / `schHeight`, and overriding `pinAttributes` at the call site for a `tsci import` part that triggers `source_no_power_pin_defined_warning`.
- `pinheader`: `schWidth` with labels, and `_nopinlabels`.
- `connector`: `insertionDirection` with a footprinter string, via an empty `<footprint />` child.

**`FOOTPRINTS.md`**
- A one-liner that prints the pad positions of a footprinter string.

## Things noticed that may be worth fixing in tscircuit instead

- A `<pinheader>` with `pinLabels` and a two-pin `<connector>` on a power rail fail `schematic-placement` with their default schematic box.
- `TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` says to rotate the part, but `schRotation` does not clear it on a `<connector>`.
- With `isViaInPadAllowed`, the placement check passes but `tsci build` still reports `pcb_pad_pad_clearance_error` between the via and the pad it sits in.
- `tsci check netlist` crashes on a `circuit.json` input.

title: Use board copper clearance when simplifying a trace
description: Adjusts trace simplification logic to respect board copper clearance requirements, ensuring that traces do not violate specified spacing rules during simplification.
body:
The gamepad's RIGHT and DOWN traces could leave simplification with 0.123 mm between their copper edges on a board requiring 0.14 mm. The shortcut solver used a fixed 0.10 mm margin even when the caller supplied the board clearance.

Forward the existing board clearance to the path simplifier. A declared copper-edge clearance uses the physical trace widths by default. Callers can still set the width mode explicitly. The regression independently measures the two traces' closest copper edges after simplification. The sampler keeps its normal spacing when that already meets the board rule. If the board rule blocks an otherwise acceptable shortcut and sampling retains original segments, the vertex search tries shorter paths under the same clearance checks.

Stacked on #69. The mounting-hole rule and circular hole geometry can merge independently. All 67 solver tests, formatting and TypeScript pass in CI.

Downstream qualification on [autorouter #4118](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/4118) found a regression on the A13 DDR board. The prior head reported 9 errors against a limit of 7 on Linux. The updated solver measured 7 in the local A13 replay. The independent hole PRs can merge ahead of this copper change.

The shortcut solver skips exact distance checks when the bounding boxes are farther apart than the required clearance. The segment lookup also uses that clearance as its search radius. A regression test covers two traces 1 mm apart on a board that requires 0.9 mm between copper edges.

Across 16 boards on dataset 18, simplification took 23.17 s versus 30.14 s on the autorouter base (23% faster). All 16 board snapshots matched byte for byte, and all passed relaxed DRC. [Benchmark results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/4118#issuecomment-7087327699)

On the full Trial239 fixture, all four loops ran with both revisions. The previous head used 0.15 mm for the width of a 0.10 mm trace, which rejected legal shortcuts at the 0.20 mm copper gap. Segments outside horizontal, vertical or 45° fell from 1,943 to 1,088. Before this PR, the solver produced 342 with the previous clearance behavior. The regression now measures that count as well as the original near-zero segment. On the resulting geometry, 979 of the remaining 1,088 off-angle segments have at least one endpoint that fails the clearance check with its existing neighbors. On `source_trace_288`, the count dropped from 63 to 7 and the path shortened from 50.48 to 48.09 mm. [Trial239 snapshot change](https://github.com/tscircuit/trace-simplification-solver/commit/277a23b3e801afb95752ca56e6626c11149e5680)

New concepts Channel simulation preparation. prepareChannelSimulationById prepares the drivers, receivers, timing and stimuli for one simulation. body:
Prepare each PCB transient channel simulation written by core. Validate its driver–receiver channels, scope the copper and IBIS models, and lower the settings, stimuli and probes used by routed admission in #100.

Stacked on #120.

### New concepts

- **Channel simulation preparation.** `prepareChannelSimulationById` prepares the drivers, receivers, timing and stimuli for one simulation. Model, supply and control helpers return updated Circuit JSON.
- **Declared and nominal supplies.** A declared voltage source stays with the retained nets it supplies. The IBIS reference voltages bias unpowered rails.
- **Pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS).** The seed determines the starting phase. Preparation generates only the bits needed for the recording, up to the pattern limit.

Adjacent routed segments may share a physical endpoint. Constant drivers hold their level from t=0 regardless of the stimulus offset.

### Aggressor states

Use `aggressorPattern` to set a quiet level or switching pattern, or set `aggressorDisabled` for high impedance. Every retained output-capable pin outside the declared driver roles needs an explicit state, including bidirectional receivers. Admission names the pins in the error if their state is missing.

This PR pins the core preview from tscircuit/core#5804 so TSX emits the aggressor fields. Switch the preview pin to the release when it ships.

title: feat: add CopperScope to select the copper each channel extracts
description: Adds CopperScope for routed channel extraction. Stacked on 158. Routed admission in 99 supplies the distance in millimetres and defaults to 32 mm. Scope rejects non-finite or negative distances with simulation_scope.
body:
Adds CopperScope for routed channel extraction. Stacked on #158. Routed admission in #99 supplies the distance in millimetres and defaults to 32 mm. Scope rejects non-finite or negative distances with `simulation_scope`.

### New concepts

- **Copper scope.** The channel’s wires, pads, via barrels and signal pours supply the bounding boxes for the search. Copper within the inclusive XY bounding-box distance on the same layer or one stack index away admits its signal net. An inner2 trace directly under a top trace falls outside this rule even when inner1 has no shielding plane. Copper without a net association is ignored.
- **Passive bridges.** Nearby signal nets extend through series resistors, capacitors and inductors when neither side belongs to a supply or reference net. The caller must include both sides of series passives in `channelSourceIds`.
- **Rail and return copper.** Nearby supply and reference traces are classified as grounded electrodes. Reference vias remain eligible board-wide. Via bounds include explicit drill limits and through-hole stubs.

### PCB snapshots

body:
Adds `getDifferentialPairPhaseSkew({ circuitJson })`, a pure function that computes KiCad-style phase skew for every routed differential pair, so pcb-viewer can draw it on demand instead of reading it from Circuit JSON.

It ports the calculation from tscircuit/core #5749 (closed) and the via length through the stackup from core #5752 (closed), with the shared contract's snake_case output: `source_bus_id`, `positive_trace` / `negative_trace` (`pcb_trace_id`, `max_phase_skew`, `min_phase_skew`, `segments` with optional `phase_skew`), `max_abs_phase_skew`, `end_to_end_length_delta` (always present) and `max_length_skew` (copied from `<differentialpair maxLengthSkew>`, an unsigned limit).

- Reads Circuit JSON through `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` (`cju`) and finds each pair's board with its `createBoardOwnerMap`. Reads the board's `thickness` and `num_layers` through circuit-json's `pcb_board` schema, so a record that omits them gets the schema's defaults.
- Walks copper with the copper renderers' layer rules: wire points on one layer, a wire point and a via on one of the via's layers, a through pad across its pad. A via joins its two layers whichever way it is stored, also at the start of a route. Two vias in a row, as core routes `pcbPath` vias, join on the layer they share.
- Measures routing inside the start and end pads, and on either side of a via inside its pad where the via's outer diameter is known, straight from the pad centre to where the route leaves the pad, or to a via inside the pad, as KiCad's tuning path does, so a jog hidden in a pad, its drill or a via's pad adds no phase skew. Pads are measured by their outer copper outline as renderers draw it (drill included, oval plated pads as ellipses), built from each pad shape's fields without throwing; each leg is checked for where it first crosses the outline (points on an edge count as inside), so a leg through the notch of a concave pad leaves the pad there however the route is split. Routing whose straight replacement would cross a concave pad's notch is kept as drawn.
- Cuts teardrop tapers into constant-width wire points every 0.01 mm of width change before clipping, so matching and drawing use the local width, also where a taper crosses a pad edge.
- A via counts its height through the board's stackup; without one, it is estimated by spacing copper layers evenly through the board thickness by `num_layers`. That is close to KiCad's default stackup but not equal (KiCad takes off copper and solder mask first: 1.58 mm rather than 1.6 mm top to bottom on a 1.6 mm 4-layer board).
- Ramps are sampled every 0.05 mm, joining neighbours with the same rounded phase skew (10 nm), so sub-micron ramps keep their gradient.
- A pair is left out, without throwing or hiding other pairs, when a side is routed as several `pcb_trace`s or is unrouted, the same trace is on both sides, a trace has no planar copper (a via in pad joining two pads at one point), a trace's copper jumps layers without a via or changes to a copper layer its board doesn't have, or its board's dimensions fail the `pcb_board` schema or still give no finite length.
- Deleted with the core render phase: the stored element and its colours, the runtime error for a failed pair, the split-pair warning, and the teardrop/async-routing ordering (a pure function measures whatever Circuit JSON it is given).
- Functions return new values instead of mutating their arguments (walk joining, interval insertion, phase skew range), per AGENTS.md.
- Tests: the TSX USB reproduction (core #5747), the KiCad-ported behaviour tests from core #5749 and pcb-viewer `fix6/calc`, and regression tests for the cases above, all rendered through `@tscircuit/core`, with SVG snapshots of the overlay in KiCad's colours.

Packages: adds `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` as a dependency; `@tscircuit/core`, `tscircuit`, `@tscircuit/checks`, `react` and `bun-match-svg` as test-only dev dependencies.

Install preview (no build step; ships `lib/*.ts`):

```bash
bun add https://pkg.pr.new/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-differential-pair-phase-skew@0836b0e
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[source_bus with differential_pair] --> B[one pcb_trace per side]
  B --> T[cut tapers into constant-width pieces]
  T --> C[clip routing inside start and end pads and via pads]
  C --> D[walk copper by renderer layer rules, vias by stackup height, tapers by local width]
  D -->|no planar copper or a layer jump| X[pair left out]
  D --> E[orient walks from output ports]
  E --> F[find parallel, close coupled runs]
  F --> G[spans: unknown, measured, interpolated]
  G --> H[segments every 0.05 mm with phase_skew, equal neighbours joined]
```

Stacked on: #1 (`scaffold`).

### New concepts
- **Phase skew**: at a point along a pair, how much farther this trace has run than its partner (mm). It is signed per trace, as KiCad shows it: `positive_trace` holds P minus N and `negative_trace` holds N minus P, so the two traces show opposite colours at the same place. `end_to_end_length_delta` is always P minus N.
- **Coupled run**: a stretch where both traces run parallel (cosine ≥ 0.9999) on one layer within `(gap + mean width) × 1.2`. Phase skew is known inside runs, interpolated between them, and unknown before the first and after the last.
- **Pad clipping**: KiCad's `OptimiseTraceInPad` and `OptimiseTraceInVia`. From the end of a route inside its pad, the measured path runs straight to the first point where the route leaves the pad's outer outline, or to a via inside the pad; the wire points in between are dropped. Routing that already runs straight is left as it is.

Behaviour differs from core in one place: a via counts its height through the board's stackup (or an estimate from evenly spaced layers through its thickness without one), as core #5752 proposed. Core main still counts 1.6 mm per via in `pcb_trace.trace_length`, so on boards that aren't 1.6 mm thick `end_to_end_length_delta` can differ from core's bus length skew check.

title: chore: scaffold the phase skew package and export KiCad's default colors
description: Sets up the package so the differential pair phase skew calculation can land in the next PR.
body:
Sets up the package so the differential pair phase skew calculation can land in the next PR.

- Handbook "GitHub-vanilla" layout with no build step: source in `lib/`, `"module": "lib/index.ts"`, `"files": ["lib"]`, tsconfig paths for `lib/*` and `tests/*`, lockfile disabled in `bunfig.toml`, `bun.lock` and `.cursor` ignored.
- `biome.json`, `bunfig.toml` and the Type Check, Bun Test and Format Check workflows are verbatim copies of `tscircuit/plop` `template-files/` (bunfig's lockfile lines uncommented, as the handbook says). CI runs `bun run format:check`, as the template does.
  - `@biomejs/biome` is pinned to `2.0.0`, the version the template's schema names. Later 2.x releases also format Markdown and would rewrite the verbatim handbook copies below.
- Packages: `circuit-json` is a peer dependency (`>=0.0.561`), since its types make up the public API of the calculation in #2; TypeScript is a dev dependency only (no `typescript` peer).
- PR package preview workflow from `circuit-json-to-connectivity-map`, minus its build step, so each PR gets a pkg.pr.new install URL. No npm release workflow: consumers install from GitHub or a preview.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` with `* @0hmX`.
- `docs/style/code.md` and `docs/style/api-design.md`: verbatim copies of the handbook guides. `AGENTS.md`: adapted from the signal-integrity-pipeline rules; it points at those guides and keeps only what they lack (one named object overrides `code.md` §1–2 context passing here, return never override, TSX tests through core, PR rules, etc.).
- README with "What is it?" and "How to use it?", including that the package ships TypeScript source for `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`.
- First export: `DEFAULT_PHASE_SKEW_COLORS`, KiCad's default colours (blue positive, red negative, white zero, grey unknown), for pcb-viewer to use when no `phaseSkewColors` prop is given.

Stacked on: `main`.

### New concepts
- **Phase skew**: at each point along a differential pair, how much farther one trace has run than its partner. KiCad shows it with its differential pair phase skew tool; this package computes it from Circuit JSON instead of storing it there. It is signed per trace, so the two traces of a pair show opposite colours at the same place.

No behaviour change (new package).
