title: repro: redundant trace between internally connected USBLC6 pins
description: Fixes redundant copper trace between internally connected pins of the USBLC6 ESD protector in PCB design.
body:
While building [UART Dock](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/uart-dock#pcb), I noticed extra copper around D_USB, the USBLC6-2SC6 ESD protector (C7519). Pins 1 and 6 are connected inside the chip and are declared in `internallyConnectedPins`, but putting both on `USB_DP` still makes the router add a PCB trace between them.

Look at the **vertical red trace joining pads 1 and 6 on the right side of D_USB** in the snapshot. The two external connections should be able to use the link inside the chip without adding that parallel trace. This is redundant copper on one net, not a short between different nets.

![USBLC6 pads 1 and 6 joined by an unnecessary PCB trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/core/ff35b140d4b29bec862ea890c7d8862369a2fc84/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-usblc6-internal-pin-loop-pcb.snap.svg)

The repro keeps the actual C7519 pad geometry and reduces the board to one signal path and its supply connections. This PR only adds the TSX repro and its SVG snapshot.

Verified on core 0.0.2463: the snapshot test and TypeScript check pass. The snapshot records the current incorrect routing.

title: Emit wire harness drawings from TSX
description: Lets a wire harness (cable manufacturing) sheet be defined in TSX. Core now emits the records added in tscircuitcircuit-json1023 from the props added in tscircuitprops1030; tscircuitcircuit-json-to-drawing14 renders them.
body:
Lets a wire harness (cable manufacturing) sheet be defined in TSX. Core now emits the records added in tscircuit/circuit-json#1023 from the props added in tscircuit/props#1030; tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing#14 renders them.

[Harness sheet rendered from TSX](`` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/0822b950f28d8830b5384ba60200afcd2f083124/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-drawing-harness.snap.svg ``)

```tsx
<assembly.cable name="MOTOR_CABLE" from=".J1" to=".J2"
  length="50mm" lengthTolerance="3mm"
  fromConnectorName="H1" toConnectorName="H2" wireAwg="22awg">
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={1} toPin={1} color="black" />
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={3} toPin={4} color="black" />
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={4} toPin={3} color="black" />
  <assembly.cablewire fromPin={6} toPin={6} color="black" />
</assembly.cable>

<assembly.drawing.page size="iso_a4" anchorAlignment="bottom_left">
  <assembly.drawing.harnessview name="harness" cableRef="MOTOR_CABLE"
    centerX={148.5} centerY={148} width={230} height={76} showBalloons />
  <assembly.drawing.wiringtable cableRef="MOTOR_CABLE" title="WIRING"
    paperX={212} paperY={98} anchorAlignment="top_left" />
  <assembly.drawing.bomtable partRef="MOTOR_CABLE"
    paperX={5} paperY={5} anchorAlignment="bottom_left" />
</assembly.drawing.page>
```

## What core emits

- **`assembly.cable`** writes `nominal_length`, `length_tolerance`, `from_connector_name` and `to_connector_name` onto its `cad_cable`.
- **`assembly.cablewire`** (new) becomes one `cad_cable_wire` per child, in from-pin order, inheriting `wireAwg` from the cable. Pins beyond a connector's contact count and two wires on one pin are errors.
- **Cable BOM.** A wired cable's `cad_assembly_bom_item` gains children: wire by gauge and colour (counted in cut pieces), each end's housing, and one crimp contact per wire end. Identical lines merge. An unwired cable stays a single line.
- **`assembly.drawing.harnessview`** (new) becomes a `drawing_wiring_harness_view`. It takes part in `leftOfRef`/`aboveRef` placement with the other views. `showBalloons` adds three `drawing_balloon` records whose texts are the item numbers in the cable's parts list on the same page.
- **`assembly.drawing.wiringtable`** and **`assembly.drawing.bomtable`** (new) resolve to `drawing_table` plus `drawing_table_cell` records with final text, column widths and row heights. The wiring list adds SIGNAL, COLOR and AWG columns only for attributes some wire states. A parts list anchored at its bottom edge lists rows upward from its heading.

A page is still validated completely before any of its records are inserted.

## Dependency changes

- `@tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing` (dev) 0.0.6 → 0.0.7, the release that renders harness views. No existing drawing snapshot changed.
- `DrawingRender` now also waits for `CadAssemblyBomRender`, since parts lists read BOM records.

## Notes for review

- **Cables with different contact counts are still not expressible.** The motivating PH-6P to PH-4P cable needs `adaptercable_a(jst_ph_pins6)_b(jst_ph_pins4)`, which cableprinter rejects, and core rejects mismatched inferred endpoints. This PR does not change that, so the example uses 6-position housings at both ends.
- **BOM quantities.** `docs/assembly-bom.md` says local quantity is always 1; wired cables now add child lines with larger quantities. Docs are not touched in this PR.
- **Balloon placement** is a fixed convention: along the top edge of the viewport, at the left, at 40% across, and at the right. Only the leader tip is resolved by the renderer.
- **`cableRef` / `partRef`** accept a bare name (`MOTOR_CABLE`) as well as a selector.
- **Notes inside a harness view** resolve to page positions, because `drawing_page_note` has no harness-view-relative mode.
- I ran `tests/assembly` locally (137 files pass; two heavy 3D tests only time out when the whole folder runs in parallel here and pass alone). The rest of the suite is left to CI.

title: Preserve hand-placed components inside schematic sheets
description: Fixes the issue where hand-placed components inside schematic sheets were not preserved during layout, ensuring correct rendering and placement of components in nested groups.

title: Recognize via annulus contact with an SMT pad in physical connectivity checks
description: Fixes connectivity checks to recognize when a pad lands on a via annulus, improving diagnostics for PCB designs.
body:
Stacked on #593. A pad can land on a via annulus while the via center and both planar wire endpoints lie outside the pad.

The spatial index now records via-to-SMT-pad contacts on shared copper layers using the pad outline and the annulus with the drill removed. This works for emitted barrels and route-only vias. The contiguity check follows geometric contacts separately from endpoint port IDs. A stale ID on a disconnected island cannot satisfy a required pad. The repro snapshot updates in place so the error overlay can be compared against the same copper.

On the unchanged four-layer AM4378 Rev C5 export, the port check drops from 151 diagnostics to 139 and trace contiguity drops from 7 to 5. Both checks clear J_LCD.P14 on LCD_DE and U_WLAN.pin11 on WLAN_IRQ. Both WLAN_SCLK findings remain. The independent board audit still has 30 open nets.

Verified the final commit using Bun 1.4.5. All 813 repository tests, the TypeScript check, format check and package build passed locally. The stacked branch also passed the hosted package preview. The regression covers an air gap, a buried via, drill-only overlap, a stale port ID on another island, a foreign-net escape, a route-only via and an unattributed route.

title: Reproduce false open where the LCD connector pad overlaps a via annulus
description: Reproduces a false open error in the AM4378 handheld circuit design due to an overlap between the LCD connector pad and a via annulus, enabling independent testing of the issue.
body:
On the four-layer AM4378 handheld, J_LCD.P14 reaches the bottom escape through a via offset from its top SMT pad. The pad extends to x = 0.750 mm and the via copper starts at x = 0.731 mm. Both the per-port check and trace contiguity check report an open across the 0.019 mm overlap.

This fixture retains the pad, via and bottom wire. Its SVG shows the current diagnostics. Moving the via to leave 0.010 mm of air or restricting its span to inner2–bottom gives two genuine open controls.

Run `bun test tests/repros/via-annulus-smt-contact.test.ts`. The reproduction records the two existing errors so this branch can be tested independently.

The fix and updated SVG are in #594, based on this branch.

title: Start new boards with a USB-C ESP32-C6 Wi-Fi sounder
description: Introduces a new circuit board design featuring a USB-C Wi-Fi sounder based on the ESP32-C6-WROOM-1-N8, including a complete schematic and PCB layout.
body:
Opening the editor or selecting **New Board** loads a USB-C Wi-Fi sounder built around the ESP32-C6-WROOM-1-N8. The project opens at `index.tsx`. Its `imports/` directory contains separate, editable definitions for the radio, USB-C receptacle, AP2112K regulator, LM4861 amplifier, boot switch and piezo. The parts were sourced with `tsci import --jlcpcb`. The module uses Espressif’s land pattern and 3D model.

The two-layer PCB measures **42 × 30 mm**, down from 48 × 44 mm. All 24 components mount on top. The piezo occupies the upper right, the USB-C receptacle is labeled **J1 USB-C** at the left edge and the module’s antenna overhangs the upper edge. All module lands sit on the PCB. A copper keepout covers the edge beneath the start of the antenna.

The single-sheet schematic separates the USB-C interface, 3.3 V supply, radio and boot straps, and differential piezo driver. Both cable orientations support native USB. Hold BOOT while applying power to enter the ROM downloader. Firmware can produce a tone by driving GPIO10 with a 4 kHz square wave.

The editor initializes the whole project for new boards and preserves multi-file and legacy single-file share links. The PR also aligns the circuit-json schema used by the drawing dependencies to fix the Vercel TypeScript failure.

**Verification**

- Ran the editor worker with supplier lookup enabled. All 54 traces routed, with zero circuit errors, warnings or additional design-rule findings.
- Regression tests cover component placement, on-board lands, physical pin connectivity, the two independent CC pull-downs, USB polarity, boot straps, amplifier feedback and both piezo outputs.
- TypeScript and formatting passed. The test suite passed all 432 active tests, with five skipped.

[Espressif module datasheet](https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-c6-wroom-1_wroom-1u_datasheet_en.pdf) · [Espressif land pattern](https://github.com/espressif/kicad-libraries/blob/d5b68fd9269c639b3a60681e00b91df33b4db4a3/footprints/Espressif.pretty/ESP32-C6-WROOM-1.kicad_mod)

[Open the Vercel editor preview](https://tscircuit-89h3nvrbg-tscircuit.vercel.app/editor). Both editor entry points expose all seven files. An edit to the radio definition survived reloading its share link. The deployed worker completed with zero errors, and the 3D view loaded the ESP32 shield, USB-C connector, amplifier and piezo.

- `build_source` on package builds, and on package releases for the latest build

title: Skip the cloud build when pushing with --include-dist
description: tsci push --include-dist now uses the uploaded dist directory as the build instead of also building the package in the cloud.
body:
`tsci push --include-dist` now uses the uploaded `dist` directory as the build instead of also building the package in the cloud.

Before this, the flag only stopped `dist/` from being ignored. The registry still ran a cloud build, which replaced the uploaded files.

## Changes

- The archive upload sends `skip_cloud_build: true`, so the registry keeps the uploaded build output.
- After the upload the release gets a local build via `package_builds/create_local` instead of `ready_to_build: true`.
- Falls back to a cloud build, with a message, when:
  - `--include-dist` was passed but there are no dist files to upload
  - the registry doesn't have `package_builds/create_local` yet, or the call fails

## Dependencies

- tscircuit/api.tscircuit.com#1238 and tscircuit/api.tscircuit.com#1237 add the registry support and are merged. Against a registry without it the push still succeeds and builds in the cloud.
- tscircuit/tscircuit.com#6058 adds the same routes to the fake registry and is merged. This PR bumps `@tscircuit/fake-snippets` to `0.0.229`, the first release that includes them.

## Testing

- With `@tscircuit/fake-snippets@0.0.229`: all of `tests/cli/push` passes (36 pass, 4 skip), including the new local-build test and the fallback test for a missing dist directory.
- With the older `0.0.226`, which has no `package_builds/create_local`, the push still published and fell back to a cloud build.

title: Use the widest merged connection width as each trace's power expansion target
description: Fixes power trace width expansion when connections share a pad, ensuring the widest trace width is used for merged nets.
body:
A smaller alternative to #4007 + #4008.

When connections share a pad, `mergeConnections` kept the **first** `nominalTraceWidth`. The expander finds a trace's width by connection name, and every branch of a merged net shares one name, so a 0.8 mm supply that shares a pad with a 0.15 mm sense line was never widened.

Changes (about +25 / −12 outside tests and snapshots):
- `mergeConnections`: take the **max** width instead of the first one.
- `convertHdRoutesToSimplifiedPcbTraces`: copy the connection's width onto each trace as the internal `__desiredNominalTraceWidth`. `PowerTraceExpansionSolver` maps it to the expander's input field `nominalTraceWidth`, which the expander checks before looking up the connection by name, and removes it from the output.
- Pipeline 9: `widenInPlaceAtSearchLimit: true`.
- Pin `power-trace-expander` to `f056a94`, the same pin as #4007. It adds per-trace targets and in-place widening.

## Tests
- New test `tests/bugs/mixed-connection-trace-width.test.ts`: with only the expander pin updated, it **fails** (supply stays at 0.15 mm). With this PR it **passes**: supply at 0.8 mm, 0 relaxed DRC errors.
- RP2040 and NEMA 23: 0 relaxed DRC errors and all other assertions pass. Snapshots are updated and the routing changes noticeably, because merged nets now route at their widest width. The Linux snapshots (RP2040, bugreport107, bugreport109, T113 HDMI) come from this PR's own CI run, which uploaded them as artifacts.
- `bugreport110/motherboard-power-full-route`: with per-trace targets, 34 power traces on nets 162–167 now reach their targets (for example 0.15 → 0.6 mm and 0.15 → 2.5 mm). The baseline expander ignores these targets, so the test now removes them and runs both expanders on that input. It still checks for exactly the same output.
- All 19 CI checks pass.

## Trade-off
The whole merged net now uses the widest width. That covers thin branches too, like the sense line, and also applies at routing time (`TraceWidthSolver`). #4008 keeps thin branches thin by walking the MST. This PR skips that in exchange for far less code.

body:
A conditional B-source current step into a capacitor aborts at 42.338 µs, and the TI LMZM33602 startup aborts before its requested stop time. This patch preserves capacitor precision and locates behavioral comparison crossings, allowing both circuits to finish with the original fixtures.

Stack: repro #9 → this fix. The repro snapshots update from actual WebAssembly output. The four-component waveform also has an independent closed-form numerical assertion.

Implementation:
- Stamp an algebraically equivalent scaled capacitor companion unknown, keeping large C/dt terms off node diagonals. Preserve weak conductances, integration history, and solved capacitor current/power queries.
- Use compensated residuals and bounded iterative refinement for real SPARSE transient solves. KLU and sensitivity retain their existing paths.
- Locate continuous arguments crossing `>`, `>=`, `<`, and `<=` in behavioral sources after a converged trial. Use bracketed Illinois false position, discard brackets after ordinary NR/LTE rejection, integrate the left limit, then restart through the existing XSPICE breakpoint path. Respect the existing minimum breakpoint spacing.
- Allow value-only expression evaluation to avoid calculating unused derivatives during convergence and event checks.

The upstream numerical patch changes 22 C/header files: 544 additions and 24 deletions. It applies cleanly to both upstream branches selected by the existing main/next build scripts. It changes no public TypeScript API. Original circuits, component values, tolerances, Newton/LTE acceptance checks, and minimum-timestep policy stay intact; the fix adds no smoothing, parasitic components, recovery jumps, or tolerance relaxation.

Validation on the final native and WebAssembly builds:
- The unchanged four-component reproducer finishes and matches its closed-form RC response. The positive test fails on the unpatched engine. It covers all four comparisons, both trap and Gear, both current signs, a floating capacitor, nonlinear exponential threshold crossings, AC gain, and module reuse.
- Original TI startup completes 1 ms at default tolerances, with all four tolerances tightened 10×, and tightened 100×, in both backends.
- All 27 native operating cases and all 10 WebAssembly cases complete without simulation errors: 18/24/30 V input, 12/24/48 Ω load, and 47/54/68 µF output capacitance. WebAssembly includes the eight corners, center, and the 30 V / 12 Ω / 54 µF spacing regression.
- Native upstream: all 58 harness entries pass. All 1,215 model-QA comparison messages exactly match the unpatched baseline, including existing reference differences.
- AddressSanitizer passes six source/run/remove lifecycle cycles and the previously failing TI corner. Leak detection is unavailable on this macOS platform.
- Lint, source and test TypeScript checks, Vite build, source/package regressions, numerical regressions, SVG snapshots, and Chromium pass. The WebAssembly build's complete source manifest matches the intended patch plus the repository's existing Emscripten/static-model hooks.
- `npm test` passes the applicable regressions, then encounters the pre-existing missing `test/fixtures/figure-10-17/tps63802-pfm-buck.cir`. No tests are skipped or assertions weakened.

Extended 5 ms validation also passes:

| Backend | Maximum step | Final output | Wall time on this machine |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native | 1 µs | 8.143839846 V | 1,042.5 s |
| Native | 250 ns | 8.143838275 V | 1,081.0 s |
| WebAssembly | 1 µs | 8.143836797 V | 1,964.6 s |

All three reach the requested stop time, with finite waveforms and no simulation errors. On a uniform 10 ns alignment grid:
- Native coarse/fine: 0.272 mV RMS, 1.312 mV maximum, 1.571 µV endpoint difference.
- Native/WebAssembly: 0.357 mV RMS, 2.144 mV maximum, 3.049 µV endpoint difference.

The full TI-model WebAssembly run takes 32.7 minutes here. That runtime remains a release concern; this is a verified correctness fix ready for maintainer review, not an unrestricted performance sign-off.

The repository reports no automated PR workflow runs/check statuses for this head; the checks above were executed locally.

The RC closed form validates the small circuit independently. Native/WebAssembly agreement and TI-model convergence are numerical checks, not a comparison against measured TI hardware.

Algorithm references: [Illinois root finding](https://www.math.ubc.ca/~loew/mech2/Dowell%2BJarratt.pdf), [bounded iterative refinement](https://netlib.org/lapack/explore-html/d5/da4/group__gerfs_gaf9908a6db85a278e5756cbded5f49819.html).

title: fix: drill through-vias in STEP board and panel exports (#195)
description: Fixes the issue where through-vias were not drilled correctly in STEP board and panel exports, ensuring only appropriate vias are drilled and improving the accuracy of the exported designs.
body:
Fixes #195. Stacked on #201; merge the reproduction first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

Through-vias now enter the existing circular drill builder in PCB/assembly exports and the existing panel subtraction path. Shared drill selection also scopes vias to their owning board in multi-board assemblies.

**Which vias are drilled.** Only vias whose barrel runs from `top` to `bottom` are drilled (`isThroughVia` in `lib/is-through-via.ts`). The hole type stays `pcb_hole | pcb_plated_hole`, as on `main`. Through vias are selected separately and drilled as round holes, so no type treats every via as a drill. Blind vias (outer layer to inner layer) and buried vias (inner layers only) stop inside the board. The STEP substrate is a single solid without inner-layer depths, so they are not drilled at all: a full-depth cut would add a hole the real board does not have. The span is read in this order:
1. `through_hole`
2. `topmost_drill_layer` / `bottommost_drill_layer`
3. `layers`: every copper layer the barrel crosses. Core writes this, and the Gerber drill export derives its per-span drill files from it.
4. deprecated `from_layer` / `to_layer`, only when `layers` is empty, because on an autorouted through via they can describe just the trace's layer change (e.g. `top` → `inner1`)
5. no span data: through, matching the drill export's default

Updates the same reproduction assertions and PNG. Checks cover openings on both faces, surrounding material, cylindrical walls, board ownership, and ambiguous ownership. A 4-layer case drills through vias (including one whose from/to says `top` → `inner1` while `layers` spans the full stack) and leaves blind-from-top, blind-from-bottom and buried vias undrilled. That precedence case fails if from/to is read before `layers`.

| Before (#201) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Missing via drill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/a84d495dd197f71f7c726aff6f03f31a49b11d28/test/repros/via-not-drilled/__snapshots__/via-not-drilled.snap.png) | ![Open via drill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/79ce969e65eac28e0d1a887df7fa66a608761500/test/repros/via-not-drilled/__snapshots__/via-not-drilled.snap.png) |

This uses the existing exact cylindrical board geometry. Panel holes retain the panel exporter's existing polygonal representation; this PR does not change panel precision. Existing alternative fix: #200.

Integration check: all three issue fixes apply together without conflicts; all 65 tests in the combined full suite, TypeScript, formatting, and the JavaScript/declaration build pass (including the font pin in #205).

Also refreshes the existing `repro01` STEP snapshot because that fixture's vias are now drilled; its previous snapshot failed the stricter Linux CI comparison.

title: fix: reverse the STEP board bottom boundary winding (#197)
description: Fixes the winding direction of the bottom boundary of the STEP board to ensure proper topology at export time, addressing issue 197.
body:
Fixes #197. Stacked on #205; merge the reproduction first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

Reverses both the edge order and each edge's orientation in the bottom outer loop. The loop now runs counter-clockwise about its −Z normal, and every perimeter edge is shared by two faces in opposite directions. This fixes the topology at export time. It does not rely on the reader to heal it, and it does not touch surface normals.

The reproduction now expects the bottom loop `(-25,-15) → (-25,15) → (25,15) → (25,-15)` and no inconsistent edges. A new case checks that concave (L-shaped) and edge-notched boards also form closed shells, in both export modes.

title: repro: STEP bottom board boundary has inconsistent winding (#197)
description: Reproduces a bug where the bottom board boundary has inconsistent winding in the STEP export, affecting the rendering of the boards bottom face.
body:
Reproduces #197 with the issue's bare 50 × 30 mm board (`export default () => <board width="50mm" height="30mm" />`, generated with `@tscircuit/core@0.0.2464` / `circuit-json@0.0.560`).

The test reads the exported STEP with `stepts`, before any CAD importer can repair it, and asserts:
- **The exact loops from the issue.** The top and bottom caps both run `(-25,-15) → (25,-15) → (25,15) → (-25,15)`, so the bottom loop is clockwise about its own −Z normal.
- **The closed-shell rule strict readers enforce.** Each edge must be used by two faces in opposite directions. All four bottom perimeter edges fail it; each is shared by the −Z face and one side wall. This runs in both PCB and assembly export modes.
- **OCCT still imports the file.** OCCT heals the loop, so an ordinary `toMatchStepSnapshot` render looks correct and cannot guard this.

**Snapshot:** the faces are drawn with the winding the STEP gives them, through `poppygl` (already a dev dependency) with back-face culling. Left: viewed from above. Right: viewed from below, where the bottom face is culled and the board is see-through.

title: Document manual pcbPath routing, the capacitor trace limit, net routing phases and placement-skipped routing
description: Documents manual routing with pcbPath, explains the automatic 1 mm trace limit for capacitors, and clarifies net routing phases and placement errors that affect autorouting.
body:
## Why

In a benchmark run with the current skill, the agent spent about 980 s of a 1385 s run in 13 failed PCB builds. Four of the causes were behaviour the skill does not describe:

- It hand-routed with `<trace pcbPath>` and guessed the coordinate frame wrong twice. `elements/trace.md` never mentioned `pcbPath`.
- Three builds skipped routing with "Autorouting was skipped because the 1mm maximum length ...". The limit is automatic for a capacitor wired between a chip power pin and ground; the agent removed `decouplingFor`, which does nothing.
- Three builds skipped routing because of courtyard overlaps. The skill says DRC errors can be ignored during development and does not say placement errors stop the router.
- One build threw because `<autoroutingphase connections>` was given `net.GND`.

## What changed

- `elements/trace.md`: manual routing with `pcbPath` (frame, start and end, vias, `pcbPathRelativeTo`, selector entries, width and via size, auto-placed parts), and length limits.
- `elements/capacitor.md`: the automatic 1 mm trace limit, what triggers it, and four ways to lift it.
- `elements/net.md`: `routingPhaseIndex`, and what `connections` accepts.
- `SKILL.md`, `WORKFLOW.md`: clear `tsci check placement` before `tsci build`; pointer from the skipped-routing message to the capacitor page; how to act on a pcb-style issue.

## Verification

Every statement was checked against tscircuit 0.0.3282 (core 0.0.2461) with small boards: the frame for a rotated part and a part inside a group, `pcbPathRelativeTo`, selector entries, via layers and default size, the capacitor limit with each of the four fixes, phase selection by net index, trace name and port, and the placement skip. The `pcbPath` example in `trace.md` builds with exit 0.

title: fix: preserve native PCB copper stacks and board thickness
description: Fixes the export of copper primitives in declared four-layer boards to retain the correct copper stack and board thickness, ensuring accurate representation in binary PCB files.
body:
A declared four-layer board currently exports copper primitives without a declared copper stack. Emit standard legacy layer names and links plus native V8 copper/dielectric and substack records, so the binary PCB retains Top → Mid-Layer 1 → Mid-Layer 2 → Bottom and the source board's total thickness.

Honor declared layer counts, infer missing counts from copper primitives and via spans, and reject invalid counts or declarations that exclude used inner layers. Circuit JSON supplies overall thickness rather than manufacturer stack dimensions: the generated stack uses nominal 35 μm copper (scaled down for very thin boards) and evenly distributed dielectric gaps. Material properties remain unspecified.

Convert the three expected-failure regressions from #207 to ordinary passing tests. They inspect layer names/order, native IDs, legacy links, inferred counts and total thickness in the emitted binary records. Add invalid-count and single-layer/bottom-silkscreen coverage. PCB geometry is unchanged.

Validation: the full regression suite, formatting and type checking pass locally and in CI. The real RP2040 motor-controller export passes 33 file checks: all 12 documents parse and validate, all project/sheet references resolve, the four copper layers are declared, and all 1,370 inner-layer track segments retain their layer. Native Altium Designer opening has not been tested.

Fixes #204. Related implementation: #206. Part 2 of 2, based on #207. Registered together in native GitHub stack #209.

title: Allow through-via antipads in poured planes during regional repair
description: Allows through-via antipads in poured planes during regional repair, enabling better pathfinding for vias in the presence of ground pours.
body:
An unbroken ground pour in the Bluetooth gamepad occupies inner1. A through-via between top and bottom needs an antipad on inner1. The path search treated the pour rectangle like a solid pad, so it rejected every candidate via in the region. The via-pad check and copper relaxation also treated the fill as fixed pad copper.

Both path search implementations now allow the barrel to traverse a pour. Other-net wires still respect the reserved layer. Solid pads, holes and fixed traces retain their clearance checks. The regression exercises the synchronous and incremental searches and both obstacle checks.

![Side view of the same signal via crossing a fixed pad and a ground pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/repair04/5e1b4a63bf7b26b30cd5be779a576558fd9e320a/tests/__snapshots__/repair-through-pour.snap.svg)

Both panels come from the regression. On the parent of the fix, the ground pour also produced the left-hand result: no path and one via clearance violation at (0, 0). The gap in the right panel illustrates the antipad that the pour renderer leaves. The solver returns the path.

The regression fails on the parent of the fix. All 194 solver tests and TypeScript pass locally. In an earlier revision of the [gamepad autorouter PR](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/4118), substituting this solver reduced copper DRC from 5 to 3 and full-board DRC from 6 to 4. The remaining routing and crystal-length fixes are covered in the linked autorouter PR.

body:
Adds the BGA detailed-routing algorithm used by [autorouter #4110](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/4110). On the STM32MP157, a full-width trace has just 0.019 mm of centerline freedom between adjacent balls. The solver aligns the grid to the BGA pitch, counts legal through-via sites, reserves exits in scarcity order, then routes the caller’s original point pairs on the supplied signal layers. Pipeline9 owns board selection, final DRC and export.

| Existing copper | Reserved exits | Completed branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [![Two pads and an existing trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/d2d3ab3ca5932098fad0c58c1914ef6aa76b4ca6/tests/__snapshots__/reserved-pad-escapes-fixed-copper.snap.svg)](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/blob/d2d3ab3ca5932098fad0c58c1914ef6aa76b4ca6/tests/__snapshots__/reserved-pad-escapes-fixed-copper.snap.svg) | [![Both surface escapes and their drills](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/d2d3ab3ca5932098fad0c58c1914ef6aa76b4ca6/tests/__snapshots__/reserved-pad-escapes-reserved-escapes.snap.svg)](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/blob/d2d3ab3ca5932098fad0c58c1914ef6aa76b4ca6/tests/__snapshots__/reserved-pad-escapes-reserved-escapes.snap.svg) | [![The completed clock branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/d2d3ab3ca5932098fad0c58c1914ef6aa76b4ca6/tests/__snapshots__/reserved-pad-escapes-routed-branch.snap.svg)](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-phase-solver/blob/d2d3ab3ca5932098fad0c58c1914ef6aa76b4ca6/tests/__snapshots__/reserved-pad-escapes-routed-branch.snap.svg) |

Run `bun install` and `bun start` to step the small example or the full STM32MP157 capture in React Cosmos. The existing copper is gray, reserved exits are amber, and routed branches are blue. The debugger exposes the stage, counted terminals, reserved escapes and routed point pairs.

The native fixture includes 710 physical pads and all 32 existing data-byte traces. The solver reserves 137 terminals and emits all 97 remaining branches. Every wire vertex, port ID and via dimension matches the pre-extraction implementation. The standalone suite covers pitch alignment, fixed inner copper, blocked and off-board terminals, unreachable trunks, the grid budget and the three visual stages.

On the isolated STM32MP157 phase, three fresh Bun processes per revision measured a median solve time of 6.43 s in-repo and 5.79 s standalone. Each solve took 2,996 iterations. title: Fit long connector designators in harness views
description: Adjusts connector designator rendering to ensure longer names do not overlap with pin numbers, resizing text appropriately and anchoring it away from the cable when necessary.
body:
Harness views drew a connector designator longer than about three characters on top of that end's pin numbers. Found while writing docs examples with names like `SENSOR`.

[Short, fitted and outward-growing designators](`` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/525721a11a81ffd510fd78e2640c737a5eb767f9/tests/__snapshots__/harness-long-designators.snap.svg) ``

## What changed

- A designator keeps its 5 mm text when it fits the 11.5 mm of gutter outside the pin numbers. That covers names of three characters or fewer, so **no existing snapshot changes**.
- A longer name is set smaller to fit that room, down to 2.8 mm text.
- A name that still does not fit at 2.8 mm is anchored at the edge nearest the connector and grows away from the cable, so it can leave the viewport but never covers the pin numbers.

Width is estimated at 0.62 em per character, since the renderer does not measure text.

## Test

`tests/harness-long-designators.test.ts` snapshots all three cases and asserts the text size and anchor of each.

## Follow-up

tscircuit/docs#1058 and tscircuit/skill#71 advise keeping designators to three characters. That advice can be dropped once a release with this change reaches svg.tscircuit.com.

title: Release to GitHub Releases instead of npm
description: Changes the release process from npm to GitHub Releases due to permission issues with npm, allowing users to install the package directly from GitHub Releases instead.
body:
The npm release added in #4 fails on every push to `main` with `404 … you do not have permission`. The package isn't on npm yet, and the workflow has no npm credentials. Trusted publishing can only be set up after a package exists.

This PR replaces it with a GitHub Release, following the tag logic of circuit-json-webgpu's `publish.yml`. On each push to `main`, or on a manual dispatch with `source_ref`, the workflow:
1. runs typecheck, tests and the build;
2. bumps the patch version from the latest `v*` tag (the next one is `v0.0.4`);
3. runs `npm pack`;
4. creates the tag and a GitHub Release with the tarball attached.

Dependents install it with:
```
bun add https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-differential-pair-phase-skew/releases/download/v0.0.4/circuit-json-to-differential-pair-phase-skew-0.0.4.tgz
```

title: Add deps/package-json-one-line rule
description: Adds a rule that a PR may change at most one line of any existing package.json, ensuring dependency changes are submitted as separate PRs to reduce noise.
body:
Stacked on #3. Adds one rule: **a PR may change at most one line of any existing `package.json`**. Anything more is an error, so dependency changes land as their own small PRs instead of riding along as noise. This comes from the same feedback as `deps/unneeded-bumps`: "why did you bump circuit-json when you don't need to … this adds noise".

- A version bump (one line removed, one added) counts as **one** changed line.
- Blank lines don't count.
- A brand-new `package.json` is exempt, since bootstrapping a repo has to add many lines.
- Each `package.json` in a monorepo is limited separately.

Changes:
- `lib/checks/package-json-checks.ts`: the rule, registered in the check runner.
- `tests/package-json-checks.test.ts`: a single bump is allowed, two changed lines are an error, monorepo files are counted separately, and a new file is exempt.
- An existing `bin`/`scripts` test now asserts only on the two dependency rules it's about, since its fixture changes three lines and the new rule correctly fires.
- Docs: README and `docs/review-history.md`.

Verification:
- `bun test`: 35 pass. `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run format:check` and `bunx biome lint .` are clean.
- Self-check against `review-fixes`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Replay on PRs Shibo reviewed last week: the rule fires on circuit-json-webgpu#116 (3–6 lines), circuit-to-canvas#327 (6–9), pcb-viewer#1226 (10) and signal-integrity-pipeline#115/#116/#117 (7–8). That includes the two PRs where the "adds noise" comment was left. Some replay runs hit GitHub's REST rate limit and didn't complete.

body:
Stacked on #2. Fixes the bugs an independent review of #2 confirmed. Most were inherited from the original tool, not introduced by the port.

Two commits, so the reproductions can be checked on their own:

1. **Add reproductions**: 11 tests marked `test.failing`. On the unfixed code, each one fails for exactly the reported bug.
2. **Fix**: the fixes; the reproductions become regular tests.

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| A bare `--pr 1` could return another repo's cached PR | Cache bare numbers per directory |
| A push between reads could cache the newer diff under the older head SHA | Always diff the exact `base...head` commits |
| A truncated GitHub tree silently skipped files | Fail with an error that suggests checking a local clone |
| `++ counter` read as a header; non-ASCII paths dropped; `diff.noprefix` broke local diffs | Hunks end by their `@@` counts, git-quoted paths are decoded, local diffs force `a/`/`b/` prefixes |
| `--checks deps/` matched nothing | Filter findings, not checks, by ID prefix |
| Deleting the only test workflow was a pre-existing warning | A finding on a directory belongs to a change inside it |
| Code-analysis results shared between test and non-test files; a parameter added on its own line wasn't checked | Cache by path + content; any added line in a signature counts |
| `bin`/`scripts` entries treated as dependencies; `expect(existsSync(x))` treated as a CI skip | Only real dependency sections count; only conditional skips are flagged |
| A corrupt cache entry aborted every run | Corrupt entries are a miss; writes are atomic; cache version bumped to v2 |
| `bun run check` was missing after the port | Restored |

### Re-review follow-up (third commit)

A second independent review confirmed all 11 reproductions fail on the unfixed code for the stated bug, and found variants the first fixes missed. Each one now has a test that fails on the previous commit:

- The cache version is also applied under a custom \`PULLREQUEST_DETERMINISTIC_CHECKS_CACHE_DIR\`, and an entry with no payload counts as a miss.
- Bare PR numbers are also scoped by \`GH_REPO\` and \`GH_HOST\`.
- An invalid \`package.json\` or \`biome.json\` is reported as a finding instead of aborting the run.
- A URL dependency is caught even when another section declares the same name.
- The CI-skip rule now also catches guards written with \`&&\` and \`?\`, and no longer flags guards that throw or assert.
- Editing another workflow no longer promotes an existing missing-test-workflow gap to an error, while renaming the test workflow out of the directory now does.
- Pure renames, mode-only changes with \`" b/"\` in the name, emoji paths and CRLF headers keep their paths.
- Editing only an arrow function's body no longer flags its signature.
- Two reproduction fixtures were corrected to exercise the reported bug.

Checked on real PRs: diffs from the compare API match GitHub's file lists for merged PRs, an open PR and a merged PR from a fork. Known limitations, not fixed: \`if (\` guards split across several lines, and the PR-source tests share one fake \`gh\` and \`process.cwd()\`, so they assume Bun's default serial test run.

GitHub-backed tests use a fake `gh` on `PATH`, so the suite never touches the network. `runCommand` now resolves executables against the current `PATH` so the fake is picked up.

Verification:
- `bun test`: 31 pass. `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run format:check` and `bunx biome lint .` are clean.
- Self-check (`bun run check --base origin/bootstrap`): 0 errors, 2 warnings, down from 3; the `bin` false positive is gone.
- Replaying every review comment from the past week at the commit it was left on, with a fresh cache: still 21/27 caught. `handbook/two-parameter-rule` findings went from 38 to 41 (multi-line signatures); `deps/unneeded-bumps` from 34 to 27 (no more `scripts`/`bin` false positives).

Stacked on #1.

## What changed

- Port the Bun CLI, audit command, TypeScript API, checks, and disk cache under `lib/` with a package binary and bundled plop config.
- Keep check rules, IDs, levels, messages, review quotes, cache key formats, environment variables, flags, and exit behavior. The port changes the source hash used to invalidate cached findings.
- Document CLI and API usage, caching, review history, and the agent skill. Port the six original test cases and add four parser and disk-cache cases using a temporary cache.
- Keep the plop workflows unmodified. While this PR targets `bootstrap`, only `bun test` runs in CI; typecheck and format were run locally and run in CI once it targets `main`.

## Verification

- `bun install`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun test` (10 passed), `bun run format:check`, and `bunx biome lint .` all pass locally.
- Compared full reports from the original and port on the working tree and on a synthetic PR with failing checks. Installed a local package tarball and exercised the binary and API import.
- `bun lib/cli/check.ts --base origin/bootstrap` reported:

  ```text
  0 error(s), 3 warning(s)
  ```

  The warnings cover documentation comments in `lib/types.ts`, the package binary entry misidentified as a dependency, and intentional circuit-json filtering in a test fixture. The existing rules produce the same warnings.
